11.8% use regional programmes same PsyEN in secondary (2024) ~3,330 , against ~4,700 in the early 1980s; up to 1,500 pupils per psy in some académies AN QE 11482 (9 Dec. 2025), deputy's question, not a ministerial answer https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/questions/QANR5L17QE11482 PsyEN target (union) 1 per 600 pupils, i.e. 12,000; "4,000 posts, ~1,000 unfilled" SNES-FSU quoted in L'Humanité 4/6/2025, advocacy claim CIO "De nombreux CIO ont fermé depuis 2015" (Défenseure des droits via L'Humanité); Charvet report 2019 proposed 1 CIO per département (SNES) no official count found, UNVERIFIED Loi Avenir professionnel (5 Sept. 2018) région "organise des actions d'information" on jobs and training; the Cour says the transfer of competence is therefore not full and entire, and asks for clarification, not full decentralisation Cour RPA 2025 via Banque des Territoires Second professeur principal (PP) in terminale (2018). - Cnesco survey, Dec. 2018: 89% of lycées had appointed a 2nd PP in terminale, but only one third had held the 2 mandatory orientation weeks (AEF via search snippet, UNVERIFIED detail). - DEPP (Oct. 2021, rentrée 2020): "il est plus compliqué pour un professeur d'enseignement de spécialité d'être professeur principal" (AEF title; the note itself was not read). - SNES ran a campaign calling on teachers to refuse the PP role (https://www.snes.edu/IMG/pdf/tract refus pp.pdf), an advocacy source. - The Défenseure des droits (2025) notes that PPs were given orientation duties "sans qu'ils bénéficient de la formation nécessaire", and that the hours are "jamais prises en compte dans les emplois du temps". - IGÉSR annual report 2020 (published Oct. 2021): the PP role is "incontournable" but "limité dans le processus décisionnaire", because pupils rely mainly on family. It proposes orientation modules in initial and in-service training. PsyEN hold permanences in 3 establishments on average. https://www.letudiant.fr/educpros/actualite/l-inspection-generale-dresse-des-pistes-pour-ameliorer-l-orientation.html - No source quantifies "few teachers wanted the role". The claim stays UNVERIFIED , although the evidence above is consistent with it. - IGÉSR synthesis of the national consultation on orientation (report n°24-25 236A, April 2025): https://www.education.gouv.fr/igesr/synthese-de-la-concertation-nationale-sur-l-orientation-des-eleves-465618 (page 403, content not read). The ministry's "plan Avenir" for rentrée 2025 aims to fight "assignations sociales, de genre et territoriales" (Repères 2025, introduction). - Teachers' knowledge of courses: the Cour (2012 report on orientation at the end of collège) already recommended training teachers on courses and job prospects (recommendation 3). The IGÉSR (2021) and the Défenseure (2025) repeat the point. No survey measures teachers' knowledge directly, so UNVERIFIED as a figure. A7. Girls and science - Cour des comptes RPA 2025: 8.6% girls in terminale STI2D, against 84.5% in ST2S. - Repères 2025: industrial courses are "essentiellement masculines", tertiary courses "féminines" (introduction, section 3.4). - Breda, Grenet, Monnet & Van Effenterre (2023, Economic Journal 133:1773–1809). One-hour classroom visits by 56 female scientists were randomised among 20,000 lycéens in Île-de-France. Among terminale girls, enrolment in selective, male-dominated STEM courses rose from 11% to 14.5%, driven by girls who were strong in maths. There was no effect in 2de. The visits reduced stereotypes, and they worked best when they did not stress women's under-representation. https://halshs.archives-ouvertes.fr/halshs-01713068 --- B. England Who does guidance. Schools are responsible, under a statutory duty; there is no national counsellor corps in schools. Element Content Source --- --- --- Statutory duty Governing bodies "must" secure independent, impartial careers guidance for pupils in years 7–13. Legal bases: ss.42A/42B/45A Education Act 1997 and s.72 Education and Skills Act 2008 DfE statutory guidance (last updated 23 June 2026) https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/careers-guidance-provision-for-young-people-in-schools/careers-guidance-and-access-for-education-and-training-providers History The Education Act 2011 moved the duty from Connexions to schools (from Sept. 2012, years 9–11), later extended to years 8–13 and then year 7 (2022) UNVERIFIED (background); the current guidance does not restate the history Provider access ("Baker Clause" 2018, strengthened by Skills and Post-16 Education Act 2022, in force Jan. 2023) at least 6 encounters with technical-education or apprenticeship providers: 2 mandatory in Y8–9, 2 mandatory in Y10–11, 2 offered in Y12–13, all in the school day DfE guidance above; the Baker Clause dates are UNVERIFIED Careers Leader each school "should" appoint a trained careers leader with protected time and a budget DfE guidance Gatsby Benchmarks 8 benchmarks (Holman 2014, Gatsby Foundation), updated Nov. 2024 ( Good Career Guidance: The Next 10 Years ), to be used from 2025-26; strengthened benchmark 6 = multiple workplace experiences by 16 plus one by 18; government aims at 2 weeks' work experience guaranteed DfE guidance; https://gatsbybenchmarks.org.uk/?p=777 Careers hubs (CEC + local authorities) 96% of schools and colleges in a hub (Sept. 2025) DfE guidance Achievement average benchmarks achieved rose from 2 (2016/17) to 6.0/8 (2024/25); more than a quarter achieve all 8; longest-standing hub members 6.2 vs newest 5.6; work experience is the hardest benchmark CEC insight briefing 2024/25 https://www.careersandenterprise.co.uk/media/dbbboivk/2103-insight-briefing-gatsby-benchmark-results-for-2024-25-v11.pdf Evidence that the benchmarks raise outcomes. It is correlational. - CEC (9 June 2021): benchmark achievement in 2017/18 linked to Y11 leavers' destinations in 2018/19. Each extra benchmark is associated with a 1.1% lower likelihood of a NEET (not in education, employment or training) or unknown destination (re-run over the 2016/17–2018/19 cohorts). The effect is stronger in the most disadvantaged schools. https://www.careersandenterprise.co.uk/evidence-and-reports/the-benefits-of-gatsby-benchmark-achievement-for-post-16-destinations - CEC Now and Next (March 2024): schools achieving all 8 benchmarks are associated with an 8% lower NEET likelihood at 16 and at 18. The data are self-reported benchmark achievement from more than 4,500 institutions. https://www.gatsby.org.uk/education/updates/new-national-data-reinforces-the-impact-of-the-gatsby-benchmarks-on-young-peoples-futures/ - Fiscal estimate (Percy, 2025 technical note): ~£300m per year NPV, £1.4bn cumulatively over 2020/21–2024/25. The NEET reductions are "inferred". https://www.careersandenterprise.co.uk/media/3wtgnnaf/technical-note-fiscal-benefit-of-inferred-neet-reductions-for-2020-21-to-2024-25.pdf - Hanson, Moore, Neary & Clark (2021, iCeGS Derby) , North-East pilot 2016–2019 in 16 schools and colleges. Career-readiness scores rose significantly in all year groups. 50% of institutions met no benchmark at the start; two years later 85% met 6 or more. GCSE effects are claimed, but the figures were not checked. There is no control group, so the design is not causal. https://repository.derby.ac.uk/item/93xy0/an-evaluation-of-the-north-east-of-england-pilot-of-the-gatsby-benchmarks-of-good-career-guidance - Caveat: all of the above is self-reported or before/after evidence. Schools that achieve all 8 benchmarks may differ in other ways (selection), and none of the studies corrects for this. 14–16 options and T Levels. In England the vocational/academic split comes mainly at 16, not at 15. At 14 pupils choose GCSE options; at 16 they choose A-levels, T Levels or an apprenticeship. T Levels (2-year technical, with an industry placement) had 25,508 starts in Sept. 2024 (NAO) and 27,446 in 2025/26, short of DfE's 33,400 estimate. 71% completed the 2-year course (NAO, summer 2024). https://www.nao.org.uk/press-releases/dfe-must-increase-student-numbers-to-realise-full-benefits-of-t-level-qualifications/ ; https://feweek.co.uk/dfe-misses-2025-26-t-level-starts-target-by-nearly-a-fifth/ --- C. Finland, Germany, Switzerland Finland - Guidance ( opinto-ohjaus ) is a right under the Basic Education Act, delivered by specialist guidance counsellors ( opinto-ohjaaja ), not by class teachers. Grades 7–9 have 76 timetabled hours of guidance (≈2 hours a week), plus individual and small-group counselling. Source: Vuorinen & Kettunen (Jyväskylä), OECD webinar, 28 Oct. 2021, a conference slide rather than the curriculum, so to be confirmed: https://t4.oecd.org/education/career-readiness/conferences-webinars/1.%20Raimo%20Vuorinen,%20Jaana%20Kettunen OECD 28 10 2021 JK RV.pdf - Intensified guidance in grades 8–9 for pupils who need it, with a personal post-basic study plan (City of Tampere). https://tampere.fi/en/education/basic-education/studies-basic-education/grades-7-through-9/guidance-counselling - TET work-experience periods ( työelämään tutustuminen ): 2 weeks in grade 9, plus shorter 2–5-day periods possible in grades 7–8 (City of Vantaa). https://www.vantaa.fi/en/node/3138 - Compulsory education extended to 18 (Act in force 1 Aug. 2021). Pupils must apply to upper secondary, and the basic-education provider is responsible for guidance and for tracking each pupil's transition. In Nov. 2021 only 664 pupils (0.01% of the age group) had no placement. https://www.cedefop.europa.eu/en/news/finland-extension-compulsory-education-comes-effect - Guidance in primary school and a pupils-per-counsellor norm: not found, UNVERIFIED . Germany. Federal Employment Agency (BA) counsellors work inside schools ( Berufsberatung vor dem Erwerbsleben , the nationwide Lebensbegleitende Berufsberatung since 1 Jan. 2019). Hesse alone has about 270 BA advisers working in schools. Orientation starts about 3 years before leaving school. https://starweb.hessen.de/cache/DRS/20/6/01266.pdf (regional; national figures UNVERIFIED ) Switzerland. About two-thirds of young people enter VET after the 9 years of compulsory school (OECD). Career choice in lower secondary is structured around trial placements ( Schnupperlehre , not verified here). https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/vocational-education-and-training-systems-in-nine-countries 1a86eb6c-en/full-report/vocational-education-and-training-in-switzerland 051e4a43.html --- D. Evidence on what works Study Design Result Relevance --- --- --- --- Goux, Gurgand & Maurin (2017) , EJ 127:1025–46, "Adjusting your dreams? High school plans and dropout behaviour" RCT, 37 collèges, académie de Versailles, 4,291 low-achieving 3e pupils in 179 classes; 2 meetings led by the principal with parents Plans became more "realistic"; among pupils with unrealistic plans, repetition and dropout fell by 25–40%; dropout fell ~5 pp from a 20% control mean (J-PAL) Orientation dialogue with parents in 3e works, but it works by steering pupils towards attainable courses; this cuts both ways for the "trop brutal" critique https://ideas.repec.org/a/wly/econjl/v127y2017i602p1025-1046.html ; https://www.povertyactionlab.org/print/pdf/node/1690?lang=en Avvisati, Gurgand, Guyon & Maurin (2014) , REStud 81:57–83, "Getting parents involved" ( Mallette des parents ) RCT, 6e, Créteil, about 1,000 families, 34 collèges Parents became more involved; children's behaviour improved; large spillovers to classmates; extended in 2010 to 1,300 collèges Low-cost parent meetings change school engagement https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/awareness-campaigns-parents-middle-school-students-france?lang=en Breda et al. (2023) , EJ RCT, 20,000 lycéens Terminale girls in selective STEM: 11% → 14.5% One-hour role-model visits, cheap and scalable see A7 Hoxby & Turner (2013) , Expanding College Opportunities (US) RCT, about 40,000 high-achieving low-income seniors ~$6 per pupil (tailored information + fee waivers): +48% applications, +78% admitted to a peer institution, +46% enrolled in one Tailored information plus removing small frictions moves choices https://siepr.stanford.edu/publications/working-paper/expanding-college-opportunities-high-achieving-low-income-students Resnjanskij, Ruhose, Wiederhold & Woessmann (Rock Your Life!, Germany; CESifo WP 8870 / IZA DP 14097, 2021; JPE 2024 publication UNVERIFIED ) RCT, 1-to-1 university-student mentors for pupils in non-academic secondary tracks heading for apprenticeship Low-SES pupils: +0.5 SD on an index (maths grades, patience/social skills, labour-market orientation) after 1 year; no effect for higher-SES pupils Mentoring is the best-evidenced lever for disadvantaged pupils at the 15–16 transition https://www.iza.org/publications/dp14097 ; https://www.ifo.de/en/press-release/2021-02-03/mentoring-program-labor-market-prospects OECD Career Readiness: Covacevich, Mann, Santos & Champaud (2021), EDU WP 258 Longitudinal data, 10 datasets, 8 countries Teens who explore, experience and think about work (job shadowing, workplace visits, career talks, aligned ambitions) have lower adult unemployment, higher wages and higher satisfaction; 11 of 14 candidate indicators supported Correlational but consistent across countries; supports Gatsby/TET-type exposure https://one.oecd.org/document/EDU/WKP%282021%2915/en/pdf OECD Dream Jobs? (Jan. 2020), PISA 2018 Cross-section, 41 countries 53% of girls and 47% of boys expect one of 10 jobs at 30; fewer than 4 in 10 in Germany and Switzerland Exposure broadens aspirations, and VET-strong systems show more varied ones (secondary coverage, UNVERIFIED against the report) https://cica.org.au/?p=2336 Cordées de la réussite (about 185,000 pupils per year) No causal evaluation yet; PSE/CNRS evaluation launched end 2024; a 2023 parliamentary report says pupils are not tracked — Large spending, no evidence https://www.education.gouv.fr/cordees-de-la-reussite-lancement-d-un-appel-projets-de-recherche-pour-evaluer-le-dispositif-462108 ; https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/questions/QANR5L17QE419.pdf Tutoring as orientation support No causal study found that targets orientation outcomes specifically — UNVERIFIED gap --- Ten lessons 1. The 3e decision falls hardest on poor pupils, beyond what grades explain. 52.2% of boursiers get a voie pro decision against 33.3% of non-boursiers, and boursiers adjust their wishes downward more (9.3 vs 5.5 points) (Repères 2025). The Cour des comptes (2025) finds social bias "à notes et vœux équivalents". 2. Supply, not only guidance, decides voie pro outcomes. Only 58.1% of first wishes in voie pro are satisfied (CAP 49.9%), against 87% in GT, and 3,391 LP places were cut in 2025 (Repères 2025). Better guidance without more places in demanded specialities shifts the frustration rather than removing it. 3. Grades decide the speciality, so a bad 3e year is costly. The Affelnet score rests on 3e grades and socle mastery, and the DNB score strongly predicts bac success in voie pro (odds ratio up to 2.66, NI 26.24). Flexible re-orientation in 2de pro (11% do not reach 1re pro) matters as much as getting the first choice right. 4. Redoublement is a family right, not an option the school proposes. It appears only as maintien after a disagreement (2.5% of decisions, of which 17% ask for maintien). Offering a structured "année de consolidation" would need a new design, not a return to repetition, which the evidence elsewhere in this note set does not favour. 5. Rural distance is real, about 23 km to the lycée (INSEE 2022). Remote lycées are more often vocational with boarding (DEPP 2023). Choice of speciality, not assignment satisfaction (85%), is the constraint. Levers are boarding places, transport, and regional speciality maps planned at the bassin level, which the Cour calls "le niveau pertinent". 6. Low-cost parent meetings in 3e work, but in a specific direction. Goux, Gurgand & Maurin (2017) cut dropout by 25–40% among unrealistic planners by aligning plans with attainment. They are a strong template for the 3e dialogue, provided the dialogue also opens options (strengths, apprenticeship, re-orientation routes) rather than only lowering ambition. 7. Mentoring is the best-evidenced lever for disadvantaged 15-year-olds. +0.5 SD for low-SES pupils, with zero effect for others (Resnjanskij et al., Germany). Target Cordées-type resources on low-SES and rural pupils, and evaluate them: Cordées reach 185,000 pupils per year with no causal evidence yet. 8. Girls' self-censorship responds to cheap role-model exposure. One hour raised selective STEM enrolment from 11% to 14.5% among terminale girls (Breda et al. 2023), and girls are only 8.6% of STI2D (Cour 2025). It should be scaled in 1re and terminale, where it worked (not in 2de), and focused on careers rather than on under-representation. 9. Give guidance an owner with time, training and a framework. The French PP role has no timetabled hours and no training (Défenseure des droits 2025; IGÉSR 2021). PsyEN numbers have fallen to about 3,330 for secondary (AN 2025). England's model is a trained Careers Leader with protected time, 8 audited benchmarks, hubs (96% coverage) and published results (6.0/8). Finland's model is specialist counsellors and 76 timetabled hours. The English benchmark evidence is correlational (−1.1% NEET per benchmark; −8% for all 8), so a French version should come with an evaluation design. 10. Make workplace exposure and provider encounters a legal duty, not a good intention. England mandates 6 provider encounters from Y8, and Finland mandates 2 weeks of TET in grade 9. The OECD finds that exploring and experiencing work as a teenager predicts better adult outcomes across 8 countries (2021). France's 54 h of lycée orientation time is "indicative" and has never been measured. Cnesco found only one third of lycées held the two orientation weeks in 2018. A measured, minimum entitlement starting in 4e–3e is the gap to close.

titre: 06 — An AI-resilience index for French post-bac formations: evidence base
texte: Research note, 2026-10-26. English. Every figure carries source, year, URL. "UNVERIFIED" = not checked against the primary text. Secondary-source figures are flagged as such. --- A. Occupation-level AI exposure indices A1. The indices compared Index What it measures Unit / data Headline result Main limit --- --- --- --- --- Felten, Raj & Seamans (AIOE), SMJ 42(12), 2021 Overlap between progress in 10 AI applications and the 52 O NET abilities used in each occupation US SOC occupations; also industry (AIIE) and county (AIGE) Validated occupation-level exposure score (Princeton record) Ability-based, pre-LLM; says nothing on direction (substitute vs complement) Felten, Raj & Seamans, 2023 (LM / image-generation exposure) Same method re-weighted for language modelling and image generation US occupations Used by Fed to rank US majors (see C1) (FEDS Note 2025) Same Webb, 2020 Text overlap between verb-noun pairs in O NET task descriptions and AI patents US occupations AI, unlike software and robots, is directed at high-skill, high-wage tasks; method back-tested on earlier technologies, where exposed occupations lost employment and wages (working paper) Patents measure inventive intent, not deployment; pre-LLM Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin & Rock, "GPTs are GPTs", 2023; Science 2024 Human + GPT-4 rating of whether an LLM cuts task time by ≥50% O NET tasks → US occupations ~ 80% of US workers have ≥10% of tasks exposed; ~ 19% have ≥50% exposed; exposure rises with wage (arXiv 2303.10130) Authors partly from OpenAI; "exposure" = technical feasibility of time saving, not adoption or job loss Gmyrek, Berg & Bescond, ILO WP 96, 2023 GPT-4-scored exposure of ISCO-08 tasks, split into automation vs augmentation potential ISCO 4-digit, global Augmentation dominates; 5.5% of employment in high-income countries exposed to automation vs 0.4% in low-income; clerical work (female-heavy) most exposed (ILO release 2023). Augmentation share figure: UNVERIFIED Pre-2024 models; ISCO-level, not French tasks Gmyrek et al., ILO–NASK WP 140, May 2025 Refined index: 2,861 tasks from the Polish classification, 52,558 data points from a survey of 1,640 workers, plus expert Delphi rounds ISCO-08, global 25% of world employment in exposed occupations; 34% in high-income countries; highest-exposure gradient = 9.6% of female vs 3.5% of male employment in high-income countries (ILO WP 140; ILO news) Best fit for France : ISCO-native, gradients separate automation-risk from transformation IMF, Cazzaniga et al., SDN/2024/001 AIOE × a complementarity index (physical contact, responsibility, criticality, need for human judgment) ILO data, 142 countries ~ 40% of workers worldwide and ~ 60% in advanced economies in high-exposure occupations; about half of these may benefit (high complementarity) (IMF SDN PDF). "About half" split: UNVERIFIED in primary text Complementarity is a static O NET proxy; closest existing operationalisation of Garicano's "messiness" Anthropic Economic Index, Feb 2025 → Observed usage: millions of Claude.ai conversations mapped to O NET tasks via a privacy-preserving tool O NET tasks Feb 2025: software + writing ≈ half of usage; ~36% of occupations use AI for ≥25% of their tasks, ~4% for ≥75%; 57% augmentation vs 43% automation (Anthropic 2025). Third report (Nov 2025): "directive" (delegation) conversations up from 27% to 39% ; first time automation augmentation (arXiv 2511.15080) One vendor's users; usage ≠ labour demand; changes every release Microsoft, Tomlinson, Jaffe, Wang, Counts & Suri, "Working with AI", 2025 AI applicability score : ~200k Bing Copilot conversations, classified to O NET work activities, weighted by task success and scope O NET → US occupations Information gathering and writing most common; interpreters, historians top the applicability list (arXiv 2507.07935; press: WJLA) Applicability ≠ substitution (authors say so); one product's users Common limit: exposure is not displacement. All indices score tasks , then average to occupations. None captures (i) whether remaining tasks cohere into a job (Garicano), (ii) demand elasticity (cheaper output can raise employment), (iii) adoption frictions and regulation. The IMF complementarity layer and the ILO gradients are the only ones that try to separate substitution from augmentation. A2. Early employment evidence Study Data Result Caveat --- --- --- --- Brynjolfsson, Chandar & Chen, "Canaries in the Coal Mine?", Stanford DEL, Aug 2025 ADP payroll microdata (largest US payroll processor) Workers aged 22–25 in the most AI-exposed occupations: −13% relative employment, controlling for firm-level shocks; older workers in same occupations stable or growing; effects where AI automates , not where it augments ; adjustment via employment, not wages (SIEPR) Insee (Mar 2026) cites ~16% , likely a later version: UNVERIFIED which Humlum & Vestergaard, "Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects", BFI WP 2025-56 / NBER w33777 Two adoption surveys (2023, 2024), 25,000 workers, 7,000 workplaces, 11 exposed occupations, linked to Danish registers No effect on earnings or hours; CIs rule out effects 1% (≥2% two years on, NBER version); average time saved 3% (BFI PDF) Incumbent workers only, not entrants: compatible with "canaries" Yale Budget Lab & Brookings, Oct 2025 CPS occupational mix, 33 months after ChatGPT No economy-wide disruption; exposure/automation/augmentation measures unrelated to changes in (un)employment; occupational-mix shifts pre-date 2022 (Budget Lab) Aggregate; early window Orr, Tucker & Warren, US Census CES-WP-26-56, Sep 2026 Administrative records on graduates, by major Most-exposed decile of majors: initial employment −5 pp , full-quarter initial earnings −13% ("comparable to graduating into a large recession"); half from lower within-industry pay, half from shift to retail/restaurants; fades with tenure but stays substantial (Census) Directly relevant : a major-level design; one report says ~29% of 2016–24 US bachelor's covered (secondary, UNVERIFIED) Insee, Adjerad & Vermersch, Note de conjoncture, 24 Mar 2026 French payroll employment Information-communication employment −3.0% Q4 2023→Q4 2025, entirely from under-30s (−3.8 pts contribution); salaried employment of 15–29 (excl. apprentices) in IT activities −7.4% y/y in Q4 2025 vs −0.7% all private employment; adjustment via fewer entry-level hires (Insee éclairage; PDF) Insee explicitly refuses to attribute it to GenAI alone (general slowdown) Insee Première n° 2120, Jul 2026 ICT-in-firms survey 18% of firms in France used ≥1 AI technology in 2025 (+8 pts on 2024; EU 20%); 58% of firms with 250+ employees; 59% in info-com (Insee) Adoption, not effects Coface & OEM, Mar 2026 (via Le Monde , 18 Mar 2026) Task-exposure mapping, France ~ 5 million employees, 16.3% of employment, "threatened"; exposure 10–15% for CAP/BEP vs 15–20% for higher-ed graduates, 25% for PhDs (press, Banque des Territoires) Private study; methodology UNVERIFIED (original not retrieved) Roland Berger, 2023 3,123 tasks in 436 French occupations ~ 1/3 of French work activity exposed; ~ 800,000 jobs at high automation risk (Roland Berger) Consultancy; not peer-reviewed No DARES, France Stratégie or COE publication scoring French occupations on generative AI exposure (2024–25) was found; the last COE work is the 2017 Automatisation, numérisation et emploi . Gap = opportunity for the guide. Reading: exposure is real, effects on incumbents ≈ 0 so far, effects on entrants in exposed occupations visible in the US (ADP, Census) and consistent in France (Insee). An index aimed at 18-year-olds should therefore weight entry-level exposure, not occupation averages. --- B. The two weighting ideas B1. Garicano: "messy jobs" Sources: Garicano, A New Year's letter to a young person , Silicon Continent, 2 Jan 2026 (link); book Garicano, Li & Wu, Messy Jobs: The Work That AI Cannot Reach , Upriver Press, June 2026; PIIE slides, 25 Sep 2026 (PDF); Markus' Academy ep. 164, 9 Jul 2026 (link). No 2025 Silicon Continent post on "messy jobs" was found; the argument is 2026. - Autonomy threshold. "The point at which AI stops assisting and starts operating alone: the finished output is good enough that paying a human to perform the task is no longer worth it." Below it AI complements; above it, AI substitutes (PIIE slide 3). - Messiness ≠ difficulty. "Coding a well-defined program can be hard, but it is still a clean task. Messiness comes from strong bundles and relationships" (slide 4). The threshold rises with messiness. - Three tiers (slide 6): - Tier 1, single verifiable tasks: coder, junior contract lawyer, wire journalist. Price of the task collapses ("a few percent of jobs", Markus' Academy). - Tier 2, strong task bundles: nurse, litigation lawyer, tech sales, shoe-leather journalist. "The threshold for the whole job is higher than for any one task." Most careers. - Tier 3, bundles of relationships: entrepreneur, senior manager, AI-implementation consultant. Authority, accountability, tacit knowledge ("a double digit share of work"). - When is a bundle strong? When splitting it destroys value; three conditions: (1) unpredictable demand, (2) production spillovers between tasks, (3) indivisible measurement of output (slide 10). Coasean logic: tasks are bundled because coordination is costly; AI cuts coordination costs, so the main threat is unbundling , not automation (Markus' Academy; Coy, Jul 2026). - Evidence offered: radiology (2025: 725+ AI models, record residency demand; radiologists spend 36% of time on scans, 2013 study cited in the letter). On Chinese hiring platforms (Aug 2024–Jun 2025), same-title postings requiring AI carry a wage premium for managers/coordinators and a penalty for analysts, data scientists, developers, journalists (slide 12; magnitudes not given). - Caveat stated by the authors' commentators: "Messiness protects a job only when it's paired with cognitive difficulty" (Coy): receptionists have messy but low-cognition jobs and stay at risk. - Education implications: juniors traditionally "paid" for training with grunt work AI now does; "universities will have to pick up training that used to happen on the job" (Garicano, via Coy). Letter: "The specific knowledge you learn today will depreciate faster than ever. Choose the job where you will learn most, but also the one where you will learn to learn." - Index implication: score a formation by whether its graduates' entry jobs are Tier 1 (clean tasks) or Tier 2–3 (bundles, responsibility), using O NET "responsibility", "consequence of error", "coordination", "contact" items (the IMF complementarity variables are a ready-made proxy). No published empirical "messiness index" exists yet: UNVERIFIED that the book contains one. B2. Deming: maths × social skills - Deming (2017), QJE 132(4) (PDF): high-social-skill occupations grew by nearly 12 pp of US employment 1980–2012; math-intensive, low-social jobs shrank 3.3 pp . Employment and wage growth strongest in jobs requiring both high maths and high social skill; return to social skills larger in NLSY97 than NLSY79; cognitive and social skills are complements in wages. Mechanism: social skill cuts coordination costs in team production (same Coasean logic as Garicano). - Weidmann & Deming (2021), Econometrica 89(6) : random assignment of individuals to multiple teams; "team players" raise group performance beyond forecast; they score higher on a social-intelligence test but not on IQ, personality, education; social skill predicts team performance about as well as IQ (Econometric Society). - Counterpoint: Deming & Noray (2020), QJE 135(4), "Earnings Dynamics, Changing Job Skills, and STEM Careers" : using online job postings 2007–2019, skill content changes fastest in tech occupations; the initial pay premium for applied STEM majors (CS, engineering, business) falls by more than 50% in the first decade, and graduates exit fast-changing occupations as they age (NBER w25065; IDEAS). Implication: a narrow technical skill is a depreciating asset; the index should not reward "technical = safe". - Deming, NYT , 2019 ("Engineers sprint but English majors endure"; ACS cross-section): CS/engineering graduates aged 23–25 earned $61,744 vs $45,032 for history/social science (+37%); by age 40, male social science/history graduates $131,154 vs $124,458 for CS/engineering; for women the applied-STEM premium fell from ~ 50% to ~ 10% (copy). Cross-section, not panel; selection into management/law. --- C. Field-of-study level mapping C1. Existing major-level exposure maps Source Method Result --- --- --- Timmerman, FEDS Note, Fed Board, 26 Feb 2025 Felten et al. (2023) LM and image-generation scores averaged over occupations of graduates, by first major (National Survey of College Graduates 2013–21), z-scores LM exposure: Maths & CS +1.10 , Econ & Business +0.89 , Social sciences +0.79 , Education +0.68, Arts & Humanities −0.03 , Bio & Health −2.02 . Most exposed majors (LM): astronomy 1.93, actuarial 1.72, accounting 1.58, political science 1.37, financial management 1.35. Nursing bottom ten on both (FEDS) Census CES-WP-26-56, 2026 GPT-4 task-time exposure of graduates' typical entry jobs, majors in deciles High: CS, computer engineering, information science, statistics, applied maths, EE, actuarial science, journalism; low: education, health (press: Fortune; exact ranking UNVERIFIED) NY Fed, "Labor market for recent college graduates" (2023 ACS data, per press, 2025) Unemployment, grads aged 22–27, by major Computer engineering 7.5% , CS 6.1% vs 5.8% all recent grads; art history 3%; nutrition 0.4% (secondary: CNBC/NBC) — check the NY Fed page directly (URL https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/college-labor-market, not re-fetched) Burning Glass Institute, "No Country for Young Grads", 2025 Postings for <3 years' experience Steep fall since 2022 in exposed occupations (business ops, project management, finance) (secondary: eWeek); no major-level exposure table found Lightcast, Strada, OECD, Eurostat: no major-level GenAI exposure table found in this pass (UNVERIFIED that none exists). Lesson: the Fed and Census results put maths/CS/business/accounting near the top of exposure and health/education/caring near the bottom , the reverse of the "STEM is safe" intuition. Humanities sit near the average. A French index will likely produce similar orderings, which is politically salient. C2. French data that can be matched Source Coverage Occupation variable? Use --- --- --- --- InserSup (MESR-SIES) , DSN + Insee non-salaried base Licence, LP, master, BUT , bac+3 grade licence, bac+5 grade master, diplôme d'ingénieur , bac+5 management schools ; employment at 6/12/18/24/ 30 months; pay quartiles at 12–30 months; by mention × establishment Contract type and pay now; "à compter de 2026" sector of activity and PCS (Note méthodologique, Dec 2025; open data) The backbone. PCS of graduates per formation becomes available from 2026 InserJeunes (DEPP/DARES) Vocational track, CAP to BTS , lycée pro and apprenticeship, up to 24 months (DEPP) Employment/contract; occupation UNVERIFIED BTS coverage Céreq Génération (2017 cohort: 25,000 respondents for ~746,000 leavers; reinterviewed at 3 and 6 years) All leavers, all levels incl. prépa/school dropouts (Insee doc) Yes: occupation coded (PCS) Only source with occupation for every route; too small for formation × establishment cells. Génération 2021 details UNVERIFIED Parcoursup open data Formation catalogue, capacity, selectivity No Formation identifier & user-facing channel ONISEP Formation and métier descriptions Métier ↔ ROME links Curriculum content, not outcomes Prépas (CPGE) are not a terminal diploma: score them through the school they feed (ingénieur/commerce in InserSup). C3. Crosswalk chain: is it feasible? - PCS 2020 → ISCO-08: Insee publishes a probabilistic matrix (from Enquête emploi 2021–23), xlsx/csv; Insee notes coding directly from occupation labels is better (Insee 8292892). Usable. - ISCO-08 → exposure: ILO WP 140 scores are native ISCO-08 (no further step). For O NET-based indices (Felten, Eloundou, Anthropic, Microsoft), use the BLS SOC↔ISCO-08 crosswalk (standard; not re-checked here). - ROME 4.0: 1,911 fiches, 14,301 appellations, since March 2023 (data.gouv). No official ROME 4.0 → ISCO table found. The DARES FAP 2021 gives a FAP / PCS 2020 / ROME (V3) correspondence (DARES). ROME ↔ ESCO (which embeds ISCO) mapping: UNVERIFIED. - Recommended chain: formation → (InserSup 2026+) PCS of graduates at 18–30 months → Insee PCS→ISCO matrix → ILO 2025 gradient (+ O NET-based scores via SOC for robustness). ROME is only needed for the curriculum/skills layer, not the outcome layer. --- D. Liberal arts / polyvalent degrees in France Programme Design Note --- --- --- CPES (PSL + Lycée Henri-IV) 3-year licence; L1 at Henri-IV in one of three tracks (Humanités & société; Sciences; Économie, société & droit); L2 double major (e.g. Maths + Physics; Économie + Droit; Économie + Sociologie/Science politique); L3 specialisation (PSL) Closest French analogue to maths × social liberal arts; other CPES exist (e.g. Paris-Saclay; MESR). Intake numbers: not found Sciences Po Collège universitaire 3-year bachelor, 7 campuses, core of law, economics, humanities, history, political science, sociology; 3rd year abroad (Campus France) Weak maths component (UNVERIFIED current quantitative requirement) Double licences (e.g. maths–économie, droit–histoire, maths–philosophie), "licences pluridisciplinaires", school bachelors Widespread; no national list retrieved Should score well on the curriculum layer by construction Evidence on returns: US evidence is the Deming cross-section (B2) plus the Deming–Noray obsolescence mechanism. No French causal study of returns to CPES/double licences found. The Fed note shows US Liberal Arts I colleges have the highest LM exposure among bachelor's institutions, because of their social-science share: "liberal arts" is not automatically low-exposure. --- E. Method sketch E1. Construction (three layers) 1. Outcome layer (data-driven). For each formation × establishment cell: distribution of graduates' PCS at 18–30 months (InserSup 2026+; Génération for BTS/prépa routes) → ISCO via Insee matrix → exposure. Use two indices (ILO 2025 gradient; IMF complementarity-adjusted AIOE) and report agreement, not a single number. Weight entry-level occupations (where the Census, ADP and Insee effects sit). 2. Messiness adjustment (job content). Occupation-level score from O NET/ESCO items: responsibility for outcomes, consequence of error, coordination/negotiation, face-to-face contact, unstructured problems. The IMF complementarity index already bundles several of these. Tier 1 / 2 / 3 classification à la Garicano. 3. Curriculum layer (formation content). Share of ECTS in quantitative methods × share in oral/team/project work and humanities; bonus for double majors and for "learning to learn" (Deming–Noray: specific skills depreciate). Must be coded by hand from maquettes: costly, gameable (see E2). Output: bands (e.g. A–E) with confidence ranges, never a rank to the decimal; show the underlying earnings and employment from InserSup alongside. E2. Risks Risk Mechanism Mitigation --- --- --- False precision Two crosswalks (PCS→ISCO probabilistic, ISCO→O NET) + task-based exposure ≠ displacement; US indices disagree with Danish null results Bands, two indices, publish uncertainty; label "exposure", not "risk of unemployment" Obsolescence of the index Anthropic delegation share moved 27%→39% in about a year; scores built on GPT-4 era capabilities Annual revision; date-stamp every score Selection, not value-added Outcomes reflect who enters (prépa/école students), not what the formation adds; same issue documented for UK LEO and US Scorecard Report raw outcomes; adjust for bac track/mention where data allow Self-fulfilling / herding signals If everyone avoids "exposed" maths/CS, shortages raise their returns; demand for cheapened outputs may be elastic (Garicano's price-theory point) Present as information, not advice; show earnings too Gaming by schools Re-labelling courses as "projet", "soft skills" to lift curriculum score; steering graduates to certain job titles Curriculum layer audited or kept low-weight; outcome layer from administrative data only Equity Penalising formations with first-generation students; BTS/BUT routes with less data Separate band for vocational routes; minimum cell sizes Political misreading Humanities near average and health lowest: index may contradict "STEM good" priors Publish method first; frame as resilience, not prestige E3. Precedents - UK Discover Uni / LEO: earnings by subject × provider at 15 months, 3 and 5 years from tax records, labelled experimental (OfS); 2021-22 release shows Computing medians across providers ranging from £23,400 to £99,600 at five years (DfE) — illustrates that the establishment matters as much as the field. - US College Scorecard: median earnings and debt by field of study × institution, API and downloads (documentation, Sep 2025). - France already exposes InserSup data on Parcoursup, MonMaster and ONISEP once a year (InserSup note, Dec 2025): an AI-exposure column could be added to an existing channel rather than a new guide. No existing tool anywhere combines field-level outcomes with an AI-exposure score (none found). --- Summary (10 lines) 1. Occupation-level exposure indices (Felten-Raj-Seamans, Webb, Eloundou, ILO 2023/2025, IMF, Anthropic, Microsoft) agree that exposure rises with education and wage, but measure task feasibility or usage, not job loss. 2. The ILO 2025 index (ISCO-08, 34% of jobs exposed in high-income countries, with gradients) and the IMF complementarity layer are the best fit for a French tool. 3. Incumbents show no effects so far (Denmark: CIs exclude 1–2%; Yale: no link to unemployment); entrants do: −13% for 22–25s in exposed US occupations (ADP), −5 pp employment and −13% earnings for most-exposed US majors (Census 2026). 4. France: under-30 IT employment −7.4% y/y in Q4 2025; Insee refuses to attribute it to AI alone. No official French GenAI exposure index exists: a gap. 5. Garicano (2026 book and Silicon Continent letter, not 2025): jobs survive if they are strong bundles (unpredictable demand, spillovers, indivisible measurement) or relationship/authority jobs; the threat is unbundling; messiness protects only with cognitive difficulty. 6. Deming 2017: maths × social-skill jobs grew fastest in jobs and pay; Weidmann-Deming 2021: social skill predicts team output about as well as IQ; Deming-Noray 2020: applied-STEM premium falls 50% in a decade. 7. US major-level maps put maths/CS/accounting/business at top exposure and health/education at bottom; humanities near average. 8. Feasible French chain: InserSup (adds PCS and sector from 2026; covers licence, master, BUT, ingénieur, écoles de management) → Insee PCS→ISCO matrix → ILO scores; BTS via InserJeunes, prépa via the schools they feed, Génération for validation. 9. Liberal-arts analogues exist (CPES PSL and others, Sciences Po Collège, double licences) but no French evidence on their returns. 10. Main risks: false precision, rapid obsolescence, selection, gaming of curriculum scores; publish bands with uncertainty, anchored in administrative data, inside Parcoursup/ONISEP rather than as a standalone ranking.

Other French/European candidates Firm What it does Status of facts --- --- --- EvidenceB (Paris) Adaptive modules (Adaptiv'Math, Adaptiv'Collège, Adaptiv'Langue, MIA Lycée), "AI Tutoring Platform" SaaS; clients incl. Open weights = can be self-hosted in France. https://mistral.ai/news/voxtral Kyutai (Paris lab; funders Iliad, CMA CGM, Schmidt Sciences) Moshi (Sept 2024): speech-native, full-duplex dialogue, low latency; Unmute : gives any text LLM real-time voice (streaming STT+TTS); Pocket TTS (100M params, CPU, open, training code Aug 2026). Non-profit status UNVERIFIED . https://kyutai.org/ Gladia (FR, speech-to-text API), ElevenLabs (voice synthesis/agents) Commercial voice infrastructure. Details UNVERIFIED this pass. — C. Evidence on AI tutors Study Setting, design Result Read-across --- --- --- --- Bastani et al. 2025 , PNAS 122(26) Turkey, large high school, grades 9-11, ~1,000 pupils, ~50 classes, RCT; four 90-min maths sessions; arms GPT Base (plain GPT-4), GPT Tutor (teacher hints, no direct answers) During practice: +48% (Base), +127% (Tutor). Exam without AI: Base 17% lower than never-access controls; Tutor's guardrails "largely mitigate" the harm (no gain). Guardrails are necessary but on their own do not yet produce exam gains. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2422633122 (ledger) Kestin et al. 2025 , Sci Rep 15 Harvard intro physics, 194 analysed students, randomised crossover: AI tutor at home vs in-class active learning Gain 0.63 SD (OLS; 0.73-1.3 SD by quantile regression); median gain more than double; median 49 min vs 60 min in class. Caveats: one course, introductory content, expert-written prompts per question, ceiling effect, low-stakes tests. The design (scaffolded, pre-written answers) is what works, not "a chatbot". https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12179260/ De Simone et al. 2025 , World Bank PRWP 11125 Nigeria, secondary, 6-week after-school programme 2024, pairs using GPT-4 (Copilot) with teacher-designed prompts, RCT +0.31 SD final assessment (ITT); English +0.23 SD; authors equate it to 1.5-2 years of business-as-usual schooling; largest for girls and initially stronger pupils. Supervised, structured, in-school use = positive. https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099548105192529324 (ledger) Henkel et al. 2024 , arXiv 2402.09809 Ghana, ~1,000 pupils grades 3-9, 11 schools, school-level assignment; Rori maths tutor on WhatsApp , 2×30 min/week for 8 months Effect size 0.37 (p<0.001), year 1 only; small number of clusters. Low-bandwidth, phone-based, structured content works. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09809 Wang et al. 2024 , Tutor CoPilot, arXiv 2410.03017 US, RCT, 900 human tutors, 1,800 K-12 pupils in under-served communities; AI suggests moves to the tutor Topic mastery +4 pp ; +9 pp for pupils of lower-rated tutors; ~$20 per tutor per year ; tutors gave fewer answers, more guiding questions. Cheapest proven option: AI behind a human. https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.03017 Strömberg, Lei & Wu 2026 , CEPR DP21577 China, one county, 26,811 pupils grades 7-12, staggered DiD, 30 months Homework +18% ; monthly closed-book exams −20% ; Gaokao −18% , Zhongkao −24% ; 81% of users consistent with homework outsourcing. The home-use risk is exactly the voice-tutor-at-home use case. https://cepr.org/publications/dp21577 (ledger) Voice-based tutors No RCT of an LLM voice tutor for school pupils found in this pass. Mathia (P2IA) unevaluated. Pre-LLM speech reading tutors (e.g. Project LISTEN): UNVERIFIED . Evidence gap: the voice mode should be piloted as an RCT, not generalised. Synthesis. Positive effects (0.3 to 0.6 SD) come from structured, scaffolded, supervised designs (Kestin, De Simone, Henkel); unstructured access harms exam performance (Bastani Base, Strömberg). The proposal's guardrails and supervised CDI use are on the right side of the evidence; the home voice tutor is on the risky side unless it refuses to give answers and is tested against an unassisted exam. D. International public models and procurement Country Model Facts Source --- --- --- --- Estonia: AI Leap (TI-Hüpe) Foundation created 2025 on the President's initiative; public-private, funding split equally 2025-26: 20,000 grade 10-11 pupils (learning app) + 4,700 teachers ; 2026-27: +38,000 pupils, +2,000 teachers, extended to new grade 10 and vocational schools. Pupil app co-developed with OpenAI (ChatGPT-based) + Estonian researchers and the Institute of the Estonian Language; teachers get paid ChatGPT or Gemini. Anthropic participation: UNVERIFIED (not on the site). Procurement form not stated. https://tihupe.ee/en South Korea: AI digital textbooks Ministry-certified AI textbooks, pilot rollout first semester 2025: grades 3-4 (English, maths), middle and high school (English, maths, computer science) Dec 2024: National Assembly amended the Education Act to limit "textbooks" to books/e-books (vetoed by acting president). 4 Aug 2025 : revised bill passed; AI textbooks become "educational materials", adoption school-by-school; ~30% of schools using them; state budget ≥ ₩533.3bn (~$385M) in 2024; publishers' investment ~₩800bn; publishers sued (admin suit Apr 2025; damages suit by ~10 publishers 23 June 2026). Korea Herald, 2025, https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10546695 ; Asia Economy, 2026, https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026062517581498063 England: Oak National Academy Arm's-length public body; Aila = AI lesson assistant for teachers , built on Oak's curriculum content, free to teachers, beta Not pupil-facing. Funding/model: UNVERIFIED on page. DfE "content store" (curriculum data for AI tools, ~£3M, 2024) and 2025-26 pupil AI-tutoring pilots: UNVERIFIED (could not reach gov.uk pages). https://labs.thenational.academy/ Singapore: SLS MOE EdTech Masterplan 2030; AI must be "age- and developmentally appropriate", students keep chances to « struggle productively » Specific SLS AI features (Adaptive Learning System for maths, feedback assistants): UNVERIFIED this pass. https://www.moe.gov.sg/education-in-sg/educational-technology-journey/edtech-masterplan/artificial-intelligence-in-education US: Khanmigo Khan Academy tutor on GPT-4, launched 14 Mar 2023; free for teachers via Microsoft (Aug 2024) Pilot: ~65,000 pupils, 53 districts (Fast Company, 2024). Per-pupil district price: UNVERIFIED . No published RCT on learning; WSJ test (Feb 2024) found arithmetic errors. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khanmigo and sources therein Lessons. (1) Korea: a national, top-down, single-format AI product without prior evaluation was legally downgraded within one year, leaving ~70% of schools out. (2) Estonia: fast, cheap, frontier-level, but by leaning on a US vendor's product. (3) England keeps AI on the teacher side. (4) France's own MIA: a 2021 call for a tool delivered 2024 = the "years behind the frontier" risk is real. Procurement design to stay near the frontier (proposals, not observed practice) Lever How Legal hook / precedent --- --- --- Split lots Lot 1 pedagogy and guardrails (French firms); Lot 2 model access via a gateway (Albert/OpenGateLLM is already OpenAI-compatible, multi-model); Lot 3 voice (Voxtral/Kyutai, open weights, self-hostable); Lot 4 orientation data (ONISEP, Parcoursup). Albert API (above) Model-agnostic clause Contractor must swap in a newer model within ≤3 months of it beating the incumbent on a public French-curriculum benchmark run by the ministry. Proposal Short re-tender cycle Model lot re-competed every 12-24 months ; pedagogy lot on a 3-4 year framework. MIA's 36+12+12 structure is the counter-example. MIA contract (Next, 2024) Innovation partnership Already used for P2IA: R&D phase then purchase, several laureates in parallel, keep the best. P2IA (ac-Paris) Outcome-linked payment Part of the price (e.g. 20-30%) paid on independent RCT results measured without the tool (DEPP evaluations). Proposal; motivated by Bastani Portability Open APIs, pupil data export, reversibility at contract end; French/SecNumCloud hosting of minors' data. Cadre d'usage; Albert hosting E. Teaching AI as a subject Country / body What Source --- --- --- China MoE, May 2025: Guidelines for AI General Education in Primary and Secondary Schools (2025) (spiral curriculum: primary = interest and basic understanding; junior high = technical principles and basic applications; senior high = systems thinking and innovation) and Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI (primary pupils may not independently use open-ended generation tools; teachers may not let AI replace core teaching). Beijing: AI education in schools from fall 2025; "at least 8 hours/year" figure UNVERIFIED . People's Daily via Henan gov., 13 May 2025, https://english.henan.gov.cn/2025/05-13/3157405.html ; Australian DoE brief, https://www.education.gov.au/download/19495/chinas-approach-ai-education-primary-and-secondary-schools/41945/document/pdf South Korea Computer science among AI-textbook subjects in middle/high school (2025). Korea Herald (above) UAE AI curriculum from kindergarten announced for 2025-26: UNVERIFIED this pass. — EC-OECD AI Literacy Framework Draft May 2025, final after 2,000+ responses; four domains: Engage with AI, Create with AI, Manage AI, Shape AI ; aimed at all subjects, not technical model-building; feeds the PISA 2029 Media & AI Literacy assessment. https://ailiteracyframework.org/ France Pix module (30-90 min, 4e/2de, 2025) and SNT hour (2027): both are literacy (uses, limits, ethics, sovereignty), not the mathematics of AI. Section A Royal Society, CNIL, Conseil supérieur des programmes Positions on AI literacy vs technical teaching: UNVERIFIED (not retrieved this pass). — Read-across for the "AI as a subject is a false lead" argument. No major framework found proposes teaching the mathematics of AI at collège: China's junior-high "technical principles" is the most technical, and even it pairs with strict use restrictions. The international consensus (EC-OECD, PISA 2029) is literacy across subjects , which supports the proposal's claim that the useful school-level content is using and judging AI, best learnt through a supervised tool in projects rather than a stand-alone course. Caveat: this is an inference from frameworks, not from evidence that literacy courses work; no causal evaluation of AI-literacy courses was found . Open checks (next pass, when search budget allows) - Primary text of the cadre d'usage (education.gouv.fr) and Lecornu's 2027 announcement (levels). - MIA impact results; P2IA cycle 2 evaluation (DNE/DEPP); Mathia developer. - DfE pupil AI-tutoring pilots 2025-26 and content store; Khanmigo district price; Singapore SLS features; UAE curriculum. - Royal Society / CNIL / CSP positions; any RCT of a voice tutor. - ExcellenceAI co-founders and funding; PyxiScience hosting and secondary-school footprint in France.

titre: 08 · Formation initiale et continue des enseignants
texte: Research for the proposal: (1) initial teacher training (ITT) through recreated "écoles normales" outside the university; (2) continuing professional development (CPD) inside service time (ORS, HSE), targeted on the weakest teachers identified by inspection. An "école normale" outside the university would go further than current law. Diagnoses of INSPÉ and earlier systems - Cour des comptes, référé June 2018 (ESPE): two-year master cost about 1.1 bn € ; « Ni le ministère, ni les universités [...] ne connaissent et ne suivent le coût »; some tracks had < 10 students ; M1 risked becoming exam cramming; recommended admissibility at end of licence (Acteurs publics, above). VERIFIED. - Cour des comptes, report of February 2023 (« La formation initiale et le recrutement des enseignants »): framework « demeure instable » since 2010; recommended at least one week of compulsory training for contract teachers, and professional licences for primary (linfodurable 01/02/2023). VERIFIED via press report; the report itself was not fetched. No figure on trainer profiles was found in the coverage. - IGÉSR 2022 , « La formation initiale des professeurs des écoles en France : une évolution nécessaire à l'aune des standards européens »: cites TALIS 2018, « seuls 34 % des enseignants français ont dit s'être sentis "bien préparés" ou "très bien préparés" »; recommendation 15 gives the MEN a « pouvoir de prescription sur les maquettes de formation des INSPÉ » (as quoted by SNESUP, Feb 2024). VERIFIED as quoted; the original was not fetched. - Assemblée nationale, Le Vigouroux and Genevard, January 2024 (reading): « L'une des causes principales de la faiblesse des résultats des élèves français en lecture tient à la faiblesse de la formation de leurs enseignants » (p. 40, quoted by SNESUP). VERIFIED as quoted. - Sénat: the culture committee gave senators M. Brisson and A. Billon a mission on « la formation et la place des professeurs dans le système éducatif » on 7 February 2024 (SNESUP). The report's findings were not fetched (UNVERIFIED). - Trainers who are not teachers / share of practice: the 2019 reform's rule that at least one third of INSPÉ teaching is given by practitioners in schools is from memory: UNVERIFIED , check the arrêté of 28 May 2019 on the MEEF framework. Criticism of the reform and of the "école normale" idea - SNESUP-FSU (Feb 2024): the reforms rest on an « attaque directe des INSPÉ » without any assessment of the previous reforms. Moving the concours to L3 will « accroître mécaniquement le vivier » but is not enough without higher pay. VERIFIED (union position). - Counter-figures from the same source: 92 % of MEEF graduates are in work at 12 or 18 months, against 75 % for all masters (SIES note 2023-32); only ~10 % of serving teachers came through a MEEF master (Réseau des INSPÉ estimate); « près de 50 % » of teachers began without seeing a pupil during their training; contract teachers were 22 % in 2022 (Réseau des INSPÉ). VERIFIED as quoted; the 22 % base (of new hires? of all teachers?) is unclear. - Implication: the INSPÉ defence ("few teachers come through us") also cuts the other way. The weak link is the large number of entrants (contract teachers, career changers) who skip structured ITT altogether. --- B. Continuing professional development in France Indicator Figure Source Status --- --- --- --- Primary: compulsory CPD 18 h/year « théoriquement » (within the 108 h annual allowance) CAE Note 93, Sept 2026, p. 11; Institut Montaigne 2024 VERIFIED (CAE, local PDF CAE/education/CAE093 Education 260903.pdf ) Secondary: compulsory CPD « l'obligation existe sans horaire contraignant intégré au service » CAE Note 93, p. 11 VERIFIED Days actually done, lower secondary 3.5 days/year vs 8 OECD average CAE Note 93, p. 6, citing OECD TALIS 2024 France note (2025) VERIFIED (via CAE) Singapore benchmark ~ 100 h/year entitlement CAE Note 93; TIMSS 2019 Encyclopedia, Singapore (PDF), p. 10 VERIFIED (ledger timss2019sg ) CPD judged useful 35 % of French teachers say their CPD of the last 12 months improved their practice, vs 55 % OECD CAE Note 93, fn 41, citing OECD TALIS 2024 (2026) VERIFIED (via CAE) Mentoring of new teachers 17 % of novices have an assigned mentor vs 26 % OECD CAE Note 93, p. 11, citing OECD 2020 (TALIS 2018) VERIFIED (via CAE) Conseillers pédagogiques 1 per 100 teachers , little subject specialisation CAE Note 93, p. 11 VERIFIED Participation rate (any CPD in the last 12 months), TALIS 2018/2024 Not obtained (OECD 403) UNVERIFIED, to fetch 2023 rule: CPD outside class hours From rentrée 2023, training to take place outside teaching time to stop lost lessons (Pap Ndiaye) From memory UNVERIFIED Plans maths (2018 Villani-Torossian) and français Constellations of ~6-8 teachers, ~30 h over a year, coached by a référent; aim of every primary teacher once every ~6 years From memory UNVERIFIED Lesson-study format in constellations Co-preparation, observation and collective analysis of lessons; « point d'appui prometteur, encore insuffisamment diffusé et évalué » CAE Note 93, citing CEE 2023 working paper VERIFIED Causal evaluation of constellations None found. CAE says insufficiently evaluated CAE Note 93 VERIFIED (absence noted by CAE) Who attends (volunteers vs those in need) No French data found. Voluntary CPD (secondary) selects motivated teachers by design UNVERIFIED CAE costing (Note 93, table 3): CPD raised to 80 h/year , estimated +0.23 SD at end of 3e for 715 M€/year ; a network of specialised conseillers (20 h/teacher/year), +0.16 SD for 720 M€/year . VERIFIED (these are CAE simulations, not measured effects). --- C. Evidence on CPD design and on targeting Study Design Key result Status --- --- --- --- Fletcher-Wood and Zuccollo (EPI for Wellcome, 19 Feb 2020) (link) Review of 52 RCTs of teacher CPD Effect 0.09 SD on pupil outcomes, close to the 0.11 SD gain from a teacher with 10 years' experience against a new graduate; tutoring 0.28 but costlier; CPD « may be a cost-effective intervention » VERIFIED. The 35 h/year entitlement figure is not on the summary page: UNVERIFIED (check full report) Kraft, Blazar and Hogan (2018), RER 88(4), 547-588 Meta-analysis of 60 causal coaching studies Instruction +0.49 SD , achievement +0.18 SD ; effects smaller in larger programmes 0.2 SD on achievement VERIFIED via CAE Note 93; 60 studies, 0.49 and the scale finding UNVERIFIED (SAGE 403) Visscher et al. (2025), Educational Research Review 49, 100742 Meta-analysis of 128 high-quality studies Effects need classroom anchoring, individual support, enough duration and focus on precise skills VERIFIED via CAE Note 93 Grenet and Landais (2025), CAE Note 84 Synthesis Intensive good-quality CPD ~+0.12 SD VERIFIED via CAE Note 93 EEF (2021), Effective Professional Development guidance; Sims et al. (2021) systematic review and meta-analysis Meta-analysis of PD RCTs 14 mechanisms in four groups: build knowledge, motivate teachers, develop techniques, embed practice. Programmes with mechanisms in all four groups do better UNVERIFIED (EEF 403). Effect sizes of Sims et al. not obtained Taylor and Tyler (2012), AER 102(7), 3628-51 (link) Cincinnati evaluation system (TES), mid-career teachers with value-added Teachers « more productive in post-evaluation years », with « the largest improvements among teachers performing relatively poorly ex-ante » VERIFIED (abstract). Magnitude (~0.11 SD in maths) UNVERIFIED Papay, Taylor, Tyler and Laski (2020), AEJ: Economic Policy 12(1), 359-388; NBER w21986 (link) RCT, Tennessee (with Jackson-Madison County Schools): low performers paired with a high performer in the same school, on skills flagged in their own evaluations Students of treated low performers +0.12 SD ; gains persisted, possibly grew, the following year; mechanism: learning skills from the partner VERIFIED Burgess, Rawal and Taylor (2021), Journal of Labor Economics (EEF "Teacher Observation" trial) RCT, ~80 English secondary schools, peer observation Gains for pupils of both observed and observing teachers, ~0.07 SD UNVERIFIED (publisher 403) For targeting: the two studies that tie CPD to evaluation (Taylor and Tyler; Papay et al.) both find the largest gains among low performers , and both use inspection or evaluation data to pick who gets support. This is the closest evidence for the "inspection identifies, CPD follows" design. Caveat: both are US settings with value-added or rubric scores; French inspection gives far less frequent and less standardised ratings. --- D. International models Country Model Key facts Status --- --- --- --- Singapore NIE , the single "national teacher education institute", « an autonomous institute within NTU » (ntu.edu.sg/nie) MOE recruits before training and pays for training at NIE; 100 h/year CPD entitlement; Academy of Singapore Teachers (2010), teacher-led (TIMSS 2019 Encyclopedia). TALIS 2024: 88 % of recent graduates rate their first qualification highly (OECD 75 %); 42 % of novices have a mentor (OECD 26 %) (MOE press release, 07/10/2025, link) VERIFIED England Mixed routes: university-led PGCE, School Direct, SCITT (school-centred), Teach First Route shares not obtained UNVERIFIED England Early Career Framework : first published 28 Jan 2019, "entitlement for 2 years of professional development"; replaced by the ITT and Early Career Framework (ITTECF) from Sept 2025 (gov.uk) Two-year statutory induction from Sept 2021, with 10 % off timetable in year 1 and 5 % in year 2 plus mentor time ECF dates VERIFIED; induction details UNVERIFIED England National Institute of Teaching (2022, run by the School-Led Development Trust, a group of school trusts) UNVERIFIED (gov.uk 404) Finland University-based, five-year master, very selective entry Admission rates in primary teacher education often cited near 10 % UNVERIFIED Germany University phase (1st Staatsexamen or master) then a Vorbereitungsdienst / Referendariat of 12-24 months in schools and a Studienseminar run by the Land, ending in a 2nd state exam Length varies by Land (often 18 months) UNVERIFIED (KMK page 404) Evidence comparing routes - IFS (Allen, Belfield, Greaves, Sharp, Walker, 2016) , "The longer-term costs and benefits of different initial teacher training routes": retention differs by route; Teach First has lower retention after the two-year commitment; school-led routes are not clearly cheaper once school costs are counted. UNVERIFIED (IFS 403), figures not obtained. - Allen and Allnutt (2017) , BERJ , Teach First impact on GCSE results: small positive school-level gains, about one grade in one of a pupil's best eight subjects. UNVERIFIED . - NFER retention by route: not obtained. UNVERIFIED . - No source found that compares outside-university vs inside-university ITT on pupil outcomes. In the evidence I know of, route effects on pupil outcomes are small next to differences between teachers within a route (UNVERIFIED, general finding of the US routes literature). --- Gaps to close before use 1. Decree number and date (JO, Nov 2025); first bac+3 session (2026 or 2027). 2. INSPÉ governance texts after 2025 (director appointment, share of practitioner trainers). 3. Cour des comptes 2023 full report; Sénat Brisson-Billon report (2024 or 2025). 4. TALIS 2018 and 2024 participation rates for France; 2023 rule on CPD outside class time (BO reference). 5. Plan maths constellation parameters and any DEPP or CSEN evaluation. 6. Kraft et al. and Sims et al. numbers; EPI 35 h figure; Burgess et al. JOLE. 7. England route evidence (IFS 2016, NFER, Allen and Allnutt 2017); NIoT; ECF timetable reductions.

Le slogan « nos enfants vont mal » n'est pas retrouvé dans les sources consultées (une pétition de ce nom existe sur Scolaxion) : à vérifier Wikipédia, Mouvement lycéen et étudiant de 2026 ; Scolaxion --- 2. Comparaisons internationales Sources transversales : European Agency, EASIE 2022/2023 Cross-Country Report (35 pays, 33 indicateurs ; fichier .docx, pas de PDF), OCDE, Review of Inclusive Education in Portugal, 2022, Eurydice (fiches « Educational support and guidance » par pays). Angleterre - 1,8 million d'élèves SEND (plus de 20 %) en janvier 2026 ; 538 547 EHCP (plans éducation-santé-soins), soit 6,0 % des élèves (+11,6 % en un an ; 482 600 et 5,3 % en 2025) (Schools Week ; Tes). - Coût : dépenses « high needs » passées de 7,5 Md£ (2016) à 12 Md£ (2025) en termes réels, 15 Md£ prévus en 2029 ; déficits cumulés des collectivités 3,3 Md£ en 2024, plus de 8 Md£ possibles en 2027 ; le financement par EHCP a baissé d'environ un tiers en termes réels ; l'IFS demande des prévisions annuelles de l'OBR (IFS, England's SEND crisis ; IFS, Spending on SEN). - Gouvernance : chaque école a un SENCO (coordinateur SEND, enseignant qualifié avec diplôme national obligatoire) ; l'EHCP est décidé par la collectivité locale après évaluation, avec droit de recours au tribunal. Livre blanc « Every Child Achieving and Thriving » (23 février 2026) : plan de soutien individuel (ISP) obligatoire pour tout élève SEND, offre universelle puis « inclusion bases » dans les écoles ordinaires, EHCP recentrés sur les besoins les plus complexes d'ici 2035, « triple lock » pour les élèves actuels, mise en œuvre complète 2030 (Education Hub, gov.uk). - Santé mentale : 714 Mental Health Support Teams (MHST) opérationnelles en mai 2025, couvrant 52 % des élèves et 41 % des établissements (62 % et 48 % prévus au 31 mars 2026) ; engagement de la Spending Review 2025 : toutes les écoles d'ici 2029-30 ; formation financée d'un « senior mental health lead » par établissement (DfE/NHS, programme 2025 ; NHS England). Évaluation nationale LSHTM attendue en 2026. - Transférable : le SENCO (un référent identifié, formé, dans chaque établissement), l'ISP comme document unique, les MHST (équipes NHS basées dans les écoles, prestataires et non prescripteurs). Contre-exemple : la judiciarisation de l'EHCP et l'explosion des coûts quand le droit individuel opposable n'est pas plafonné. Italie - 377 000 élèves avec handicap (4,8 % des inscrits, quasi-doublement en dix ans) en 2024-25 ; plus de 261 000 insegnanti di sostegno (enseignants de soutien, cœur du modèle italien de pleine inclusion depuis 1977), 78 % spécialisés (63 % en 2019-20) mais 57 000 sans spécialisation ; 59,7 % des élèves ont changé d'enseignant de soutien dans l'année ; 85 000 assistants (ISTAT, 27 mai 2026). - Part des CDD parmi les enseignants de soutien : de 4,19 % (2010-11) à 46,18 % (2023-24), relevée par le Comité européen des droits sociaux (L'Indipendente, déc. 2025). L'Osservatorio CPI (Cottarelli, jan. 2025) note l'absence d'évaluation d'efficacité (OCPI). - Transférable : la réponse est un enseignant co-intervenant en classe plutôt qu'un accompagnant individuel (le Cnesco 2026 cite l'Italie en référence, IGESR-IGAS 2026). Limite : précarité et turnover équivalents à ceux des AESH. Finlande - Modèle à trois paliers (soutien général, intensifié, spécial) : 26 % des élèves du fondamental en soutien intensifié ou spécial en 2024 (16 % intensifié, 10 % spécial) ; 35 % en incluant l'enseignement spécialisé à temps partiel (Statistics Finland, 2024 ; 2025). Le modèle à trois paliers a été remplacé par une nouvelle législation au 1er août 2025 (contenu à vérifier). - Clé du système : l'école décide elle-même des deux premiers paliers (pas de dossier externe) ; seule la décision de soutien spécial est administrative. - Loi sur le bien-être des élèves (1287/2013) : droit à un psychologue et un kuraattori (travailleur social scolaire) dans chaque école ; dotation minimale légale 1 kuraattori pour 670 élèves et 1 psychologue pour 780 (loi 2021, en vigueur 1er janvier 2022 et 1er août 2023), rendez-vous sous 7 jours ouvrés (Valtioneuvosto ; HE 165/2021). Depuis 2023, ces services sont organisés par les régions de bien-être (santé), pas par les communes-écoles ; l'ordre des psychologues signale que les régions ne garantissent pas les effectifs légaux (Psykologiliitto, 2024). - Transférable : le découplage (l'école prescrit le soutien de palier 1 et 2 sans évaluation externe), les ratios légaux de psychologues, le délai opposable de 7 jours. Portugal - Décret-loi 54/2018 : abandon des catégories de handicap, approche multi-paliers (mesures universelles, sélectives, additionnelles) décidées par une équipe pluridisciplinaire de l'école (EMAEI) ; l'OCDE (2022) salue la méthode (évaluation décennale puis consultation nationale) mais relève un système « encore principalement orienté vers les élèves à besoins spéciaux », des lacunes de gouvernance, de financement et de formation (OCDE, 2022). Évaluation PESSOAS 2030 (2025) et projet de révision du régime en cours (Portugal.gov). - Transférable : un cadre légal unique couvrant tous les besoins éducatifs particuliers, sans diagnostic préalable pour les deux premiers paliers. Pays-Bas - Passend onderwijs (2014) : les écoles sont regroupées en partenariats régionaux (samenwerkingsverbanden) dotés d'un budget fermé et d'une obligation d'accueil (« zorgplicht ») ; le financement suit le partenariat, pas l'élève. Évaluation NRO 2014-2020 : organisation du soutien améliorée, effets peu visibles pour parents et enseignants ; la réforme ne visait pas à réduire le spécialisé des clusters 3-4 (NJi ; rapport sectoriel 2020). - Transférable : enveloppe fermée et responsabilité collective, le vrai « découplage » budgétaire ; limite : opacité pour les familles. Québec et Australie - Québec : 255 843 élèves HDAA en 2021-22, dont 200 971 en classe ordinaire ; plan d'intervention sans diagnostic obligatoire ; taux en classe ordinaire 68,6 % (préscolaire), 83,4 % (primaire), 74,1 % (secondaire) (Bibliothèque de l'Assemblée nationale du Québec ; OPHQ 2025). - Australie, interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 16 ans (en vigueur 10 décembre 2025) : 4,7 millions de comptes désactivés ou restreints à la mi-décembre (chiffres préliminaires eSafety, 16 janvier 2026) ; eSafety a mis cinq plateformes en demeure le 31 mars 2026 ; évaluation à trois mois rapportée par la presse : possession d'un compte passée de 52,4 % à 42,1 %, usage de 85,9 % à 81,5 % (à vérifier dans la publication eSafety) (PM Australie ; eSafety ; Mediaweek). - Transférable : le plan d'intervention québécois décidé par l'école sans diagnostic ; sur les écrans, l'Australie fournit le premier test grandeur nature, mais aucun effet sur la santé mentale n'est encore mesuré. Danemark et Scandinavie (santé scolaire communale) - Service de santé communal pour tous les 6-16 ans, une infirmière rattachée à chaque école ; examen médical obligatoire à l'entrée et à la sortie, entretiens de santé réguliers entre les deux, prise de rendez-vous via la plateforme Aula (sundhed.dk ; Aarhus ; Eurydice Danemark). Finlande : santé scolaire également hors ministère de l'Éducation (régions de bien-être depuis 2023, STM). - Transférable : c'est le précédent direct de la proposition du groupe (santé scolaire portée par le système de santé, présente physiquement dans l'école). Point de vigilance tiré de la Finlande 2023 : le transfert institutionnel ne garantit pas les effectifs. --- 3. Ce que dit la recherche Inclusion : effets sur les élèves et sur les pairs - Danemark (Rangvid, Economics of Education Review 2019) : le retour en classe ordinaire d'élèves issus du spécialisé réduit les gains de test des pairs de 0,04 écart-type pendant la réforme, effet nul hors réforme avec effets fixes élève ; les élèves de retour gagnent fortement en maths (VIVE ; EER). Kristoffersen et al. (IZA DP 8823) : un camarade « potentiellement perturbateur » de plus baisse les résultats des pairs de 1,7 à 2,3 % d'écart-type (IZA). Les effets de pairs négatifs existent mais sont petits et dépendent de l'accompagnement. - France : la recherche citée par le Cnesco (Toullec-Théry 2019, 2023) trouve que l'AESH individuel réduit le stress de l'enseignant plus qu'il n'améliore les progrès ou l'autonomie de l'élève ; les élèves en situation de handicap en milieu ordinaire se disent plus stressés, moins soutenus par leurs pairs, plus exposés au harcèlement (DEPP 2023, 2025b). L'« autorégulation » (dispositifs TND depuis 2024) montre des effets positifs sur le climat scolaire (Cnesco 2026). - Formation des enseignants : pas de méta-analyse causale robuste trouvée ; les études corrélationnelles (IFOP 2023, TALIS 2024) montrent que les enseignants formés perçoivent mieux l'inclusion et sont moins stressés. À traiter comme un prérequis plutôt que comme une politique évaluée. Premiers secours en santé mentale (PSSM / MHFA) - Revue Cochrane 2023 (21 essais, 22 604 participants) : effets sur les connaissances et attitudes des formés, mais « peu ou pas d'effet » sur la santé mentale des formés ou des personnes aidées, avec une certitude très faible ; beaucoup d'essais ne mesurent pas les bons résultats (Cochrane CD013127). - Méta-analyses antérieures : Hadlaczky et al. 2014 : Δ = 0,56 sur les connaissances, 0,28 sur les attitudes, 0,25 sur les comportements d'aide ; Morgan et al. 2018 (18 essais, 5 936 participants) : effets petits à modérés jusqu'à 6 mois, incertains à 12 mois, conflit d'intérêts déclaré avec les fondateurs du programme (PLoS ONE 2018). Revue 2026 du Youth MHFA en milieu scolaire : gains de littératie à court terme, barrières de turnover et d'absence de relais de soin (PMC 2026). - Lecture pour la note : rendre PSSM obligatoire en formation initiale améliore le repérage, pas la santé mentale des élèves si l'aval (PsyEN, CMP, maisons des adolescents) est saturé. Coût unitaire PSSM France : 2 jours, environ 250 à 300 euros par stagiaire (à vérifier auprès de PSSM France). Programmes universels en milieu scolaire : ce qui marche et ce qui se retourne - MYRIAD (Kuyken et al., Evidence-Based Mental Health 2022) : 8 376 élèves de 10-14 ans, 84 écoles britanniques ; la pleine conscience universelle n'a eu aucun effet supérieur à l'enseignement habituel ; scores légèrement pires (dépression, hyperactivité) chez les élèves déjà à risque ; effets sur le climat scolaire disparus à un an ; les auteurs concluent que le programme « n'est pas indiqué comme intervention universelle » (UCL open access). - Foulkes, Andrews, Reardon et Stringaris (Nature Mental Health 2024 ; revue 2025) : les interventions universelles ont en moyenne de petits effets positifs à court terme, mais plusieurs essais de qualité montrent des effets négatifs ; même petits, ils deviennent coûteux une fois généralisés ; revue 2026 (Yao et al.) : 17 études sur 58 signalent au moins un effet délétère (PMC ; UCL). - Lecture : privilégier le repérage et l'accès rapide au soin (modèle MHST, ratios finlandais) plutôt que des programmes universels de bien-être, et conditionner toute généralisation à un essai contrôlé. Écrans et santé mentale - Preuves causales les plus solides : Braghieri, Levy et Makarin (AER 2022) exploitent le déploiement échelonné de Facebook dans les universités américaines : dégradation de la santé mentale, concentrée sur la dépression, environ 24 % de la hausse observée, mécanisme de comparaison sociale (AER). Orben, Przybylski, Blakemore et Kievit (Nature Communications 2022) : fenêtres de sensibilité à l'usage des réseaux sociaux, filles 11-13 ans, garçons 14-15 ans, les deux à 19 ans (lien à vérifier : doi 10.1038/s41467-022-29296-3). - Débat : Haidt (The Anxious Generation, 2024) défend un effet de génération ; Orben et Przybylski répondent que les corrélations moyennes sont très faibles et bidirectionnelles, et que « temps d'écran » est une mesure trop grossière ; le signal le plus net concerne les réseaux sociaux chez les adolescentes (Platformer ; Frontiers 2020, Haidt et Twenge). - France : commission « Enfants et écrans » (Benyamina, Mouton, 30 avril 2024, 29 recommandations à appliquer ensemble) : pas d'écran avant 3 ans, pas de téléphone avant 11, pas de réseaux sociaux avant 15 (Vie-publique, PDF). « Portable en pause » généralisé à tous les collèges publics en 2025-26 après une expérimentation dans près de 200 collèges ; bilan ministériel (80 % d'avis favorables) sans évaluation indépendante, demandée au Sénat en décembre 2025 (BO n°28, 10 juil. 2025 ; QE Sénat Bonhomme). Le carnet de santé 2025 porte les repères 3-6-9-12-15 (réponse ministérielle, avril 2026). - Grégoire Borst (LaPsyDÉ, CNRS, Université Paris Cité) est intervenu dans le cycle « Enfance en débat » du ministère des Solidarités sur les écrans (septembre 2025) et sur le jeu (juin 2026) (solidarites.gouv.fr). Le colloque du ministère de la Santé « Grandir et vivre avec les écrans : quels impacts sur la santé mentale » est en replay (YouTube iDPVybbT6J8) ; date et intervenants à vérifier. Chatbots d'IA et adolescents - Usage : Common Sense Media (16 juillet 2025) : près de 3 adolescents américains sur 4 ont utilisé un compagnon IA, la moitié régulièrement, un tiers a préféré l'IA à un humain pour une conversation sérieuse, un quart a partagé des informations personnelles (Common Sense). Stanford/Common Sense (août 2025) : il est facile d'obtenir des contenus inappropriés de Character.AI, Nomi et Replika en se faisant passer pour un adolescent (Stanford). - Sécurité : McBain et al. (RAND, Psychiatric Services, août 2025, financé par le NIMH) : sur 30 questions liées au suicide, ChatGPT, Claude et Gemini refusent les plus risquées mais répondent de façon incohérente aux questions intermédiaires ; pas de test multi-tours (RAND). - Contentieux et régulation : plainte Raine contre OpenAI (août 2025), sept plaintes supplémentaires en novembre 2025 ; Character.AI et Google ont réglé plusieurs affaires de suicides d'adolescents en janvier 2026 (termes confidentiels) (Yahoo/AP). Californie SB 243 (1er janvier 2026) : obligation de rappel qu'on parle à une IA, protocole de crise, pause toutes les 3 heures pour les mineurs, rapport annuel des idées suicidaires détectées, droit d'action privé (CalMatters) ; New York, loi sur les compagnons IA au 5 novembre 2025. France : rapport Élysée « IA générative et vulnérabilités » (nov. 2026, dans le dossier). Aucune étude causale sur l'effet des chatbots sur la santé mentale adolescente n'a été trouvée : le champ repose sur des audits, des enquêtes d'usage et des affaires judiciaires. --- 5.
