titre: Milburn review of young people and work: recommendations, responses, France comparison
texte: GT Éducation research file, 18 November 2026. Claude (WebSearch/WebFetch + full report PDF read locally). Status labels. [P] = checked against a primary source (page given). [Press] = press or think-tank summary only. UNVERIFIED = not confirmed. Main sources - Report: Milburn, From a Welfare State to a Working State: a new settlement for the next generation , DWP, 17 Nov 2026, 278-page PDF: https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6afb1fc5ccb3ea58ac8743c1/from-a-welfare-state-to-a-working-state-full-report.pdf. Page numbers below are the printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 9). The Analytical Annex was not read. - Government: Oral statement, Pat McFadden, 17 Nov 2026: https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/work-and-pensions-secretary-statement-on-the-milburn-review-into-young-people-and-work ; DWP press release, 17 Nov 2026: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/government-commits-to-new-settlement-for-young-people-and-to-invest-in-success-rather-than-pay-for-failure ; DWP release, 14 Nov 2026: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/90000-young-people-furthest-from-work-to-be-given-guaranteed-job-no-matter-where-they-live - Blocked: the written statement HCWS479 (questions-statements.parliament.uk and commonsbusiness.parliament.uk returned 403). I used the GOV.UK text of the oral statement in its place. The IFS response also returned 403 (see section 3). 1. Checking the claims in the brief Claim Verdict Source --- --- --- Final report published 17 Nov 2026 [P] True GOV.UK publication page "Opportunity and Support Guarantee backed by law" [P] Recommended by Milburn (statutory, p.21). Government "supports" it. Detailed proposals come in a White Paper "in the new year", with legislation after that. No bill yet Oral statement 17 Nov Jobs Guarantee GB-wide from end Nov 2026 [P] True. 18-24, on Universal Credit, looking for work; "up to 25 hours" a week for 6 months at the relevant minimum wage, fully funded DWP 14 Nov 12-month eligibility from April 2027 [P] True (currently 18 months). The UC health group can join voluntarily from April 2027 DWP 14 Nov; oral statement 90,000+ by March 2029 [P] True DWP 14 Nov AI Youth Observatory [P] Milburn proposal only (p.72-73). Not in the government statement or the two DWP releases Report; GOV.UK pages 270,000 under-25 apprenticeship starts a year by 2036 [P] Milburn proposal only ("rising towards 270,000", p.9 and p.16-17). Not adopted Same Faster access to Talking Therapies [P] Milburn proposal only (fast-track for NEETs with a participation plan, p.18). Not mentioned in the government response Same £3,000 "per hire" [P] Precision needed: £3,000 is an employer hiring payment for roles taken up after 6 months, separate from the fully funded 6-month job DWP 14 Nov 2. The report 2.1 Headline diagnosis Figure Value Date / comparison Source --- --- --- --- NEET 16-24, UK 981,000, 13.0% Apr-Jun 2026. +30,000 on the year, -30,000 on the quarter. Men 13.7%, women 12.3%. 588,000 inactive, 393,000 unemployed [P] ONS, 27 Aug 2026: https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peoplenotinwork/unemployment/bulletins/youngpeoplenotineducationemploymentortrainingneet/august2026 NEET peak about 1.01 million, 13.5% Jan-Mar 2026 (derived from the ONS quarterly change; press gives 1,012,000) [Press] Next ONS release Not yet published on 18 Nov (the November 2026 URL returns 404) "One in eight"; "six in ten have never had a job" Report cites ONS 2026 and the interim report [P] p.4 NEET rate barely below 10% for 25 years [P] p.5 16-17 NEET, England nearly 57,000, despite the legal duty to participate to 18 [P] p.8 Health 28.4% of NEETs cite disability or ill health as the main reason. Over half self-report a health condition DWP 2026, DfE 2026 [P] p.120 Mental health trend Share of disabled NEETs citing mental health as main condition: 24.3% (2011) → 42.6% (2025) YFF 2025 [P] p.120 Review survey (~3,000, two thirds NEET) 48% of NEETs report a long-term condition vs 25% of non-NEETs. 73% want work, education or training [P] p.36-39 AI anxiety Youth Voice Census 2026: 69% had used AI; 55% say tech change makes them uncertain; 19% think it will create more opportunities [P] p.37 Cost of NEETs about £125bn a year, of which almost £22bn fiscal interim report [P] p.30 Spending ratio £25 on benefits for every £1 on employment support (2024/25). Target £2:£1 in 10 years [P] p.25 International NEET 15-24 in 2025: UK 13.6%, Denmark 11.0% (OECD). Netherlands close to 4% [P] p.31, p.160 Past investment Youth Guarantee (£600m a year) = 17% of the Youth Training Scheme and 46% of the New Deal for Young People, 2026 prices [P] p.219 2.2 Recommendations The report does not number its recommendations (p.10). My grouping follows the executive summary (p.4-35). Status: A = accepted (in principle), C = under consideration (White Paper 2027, alongside the Timms review), N = no response found. No recommendation was explicitly rejected. Recommendation (target) Cost / figure Status Page --- --- --- --- --- 1 National ambition: NEET rate ~5% by 2036 ("NEET Zero"); no 16-17 year-old NEET Modelled: 6.8% (baseline 13.4%) C 8, 31, 226 2 Opportunity Guarantee in law: job, FE place, apprenticeship, placement up to 12 weeks, civic service, business help (every NEET 18-24, whatever their benefit status) in £5.8bn A (principle) 21-22 3 Support Guarantee in law: health, employment, practical help A (principle) 21 4 Paid 6-month job backstop after 12 months NEET (now 18) A for UC claimants from Apr 2027 (narrower than Milburn) 22-23 5 Youth Opportunity Service everywhere in England: adviser within 14 days, Participation Plan within 4 weeks, by 2029; mayors own 16-24 participation; multi-year Participation Agreements A in substance ("locally led youth services" from 2027) 23, 27-28 6 Central coordinating function A : Youth Opportunities Unit reporting to the PM 27 7 Duty to engage; Youth Allowance lost after persistent refusal ("sanctions should be rare") C 23 8 New Youth Allowance at under-25 UC rate; abolish UC health top-up and WCA for the young; local disability fund; Additional Cost Allowance replaces PIP; Severe and Complex Needs Insurance Savings £3.6bn/yr in 2036/37 (£13.7bn cumulative); "not pain-free" C (Timms review, White Paper) 24-25 9 Employer payment £3,000 after 6 months NEET (incl. 314,000 "hidden" NEETs off benefits), +£2,000 high barriers, +£2,000 firms under 50; apprenticeship payment £2,500 ~£1.1bn/yr; 170,000 opportunities N (£3,000 exists for UC claimants) 12 10 Employer NI threshold £5,000 to £10,000 for 21-24s in retail/hospitality, "when fiscal conditions allow" N , no commitment [Press] 11 11 Statutory Youth Opportunity Test ; Youth Employment Cost Index; public sector youth hiring (11% of Civil Service entry staff aged 16-24 by 2032); youth hiring in procurement above £5m; employer movement "First Chance" N 11-13 12 Schools: mandatory Risk of NEET Indicator (RONI) tools; statutory work-experience duty ; ready-for-work standard inspected by Ofsted; published school destination measure ; KS3 literacy/numeracy/oracy check; 14-19 framework in 10 years N / C (curriculum) 14-15 13 FE/HE: +150,000 18-24s a year in post-18 FE; outcome-linked college funding; HE earnings data published prominently; £50/week Care Leaver allowance N 15-16 14 Apprenticeships as top skills priority: 35% of a cohort starting by 25; ~270,000 under-25 starts a year by 2036 ; 25,000 pre-apprenticeships; 100% Levy funding for under-25s N 16-17 15 Mental health: digital front door; fast-track Talking Therapies , counselling, vocational rehab within 3 months (NEETs with a plan); IPS-Y nationwide; maximum waiting times by 2028; fit-note reform; legal NEET duty for ICBs; NHS 10% of entry vacancies to NEETs 359,000 18-25s referred to Talking Therapies in 2025/26 N 18-20 16 AI Youth Observatory (possibly in the AI Economics Institute): annual report on shrinking entry routes by sector and place; AI skills for every young person; retraining pilots (call centres); publicly supported firms must explain how they replace lost entry pipelines N 72-73 17 Funding: £500m in 2027/28 by reprioritisation, rising to £5.8bn/yr by 2036/37, offset by £3.6bn welfare savings and £2.4bn tax/benefit effects; 440,000 more in sustained work; +0.4% GDP C (2027 Spending Review) 25, 30-31 3. The debate around it Government [P]: it agrees with the "core principles" and supports the guarantee and local delivery. It is creating a Youth Opportunities Unit, will publish a White Paper in the new year and legislate afterwards, and will weigh the report with the Timms review. It cites the existing Youth Guarantee (£2.5bn; "nearly one million" young people; up to 500,000 opportunities) and £3.5bn for disability employment support. Not addressed: the National Insurance cut, the Youth Allowance and PIP replacement, the Talking Therapies fast-track, the AI Observatory and the 270,000 target. Parties - Conservatives (Helen Whately, shadow DWP secretary): back tighter rules for anxiety, ADHD and depression claims, but oppose "a massive expansion in the size and responsibilities of the state". She notes that savings are only £3.6bn against the party's pledge of up to £36bn of welfare cuts. [Press] City AM, 17 Nov 2026: https://www.cityam.com/massive-expansion-of-the-state-milburn-report-sows-tory-and-labour-division-on-welfare/ - Reform UK : Danny Kruger is reported as "encouraged" by stricter benefits for young people. No formal statement found. [Press, UNVERIFIED as to date and context] - Liberal Democrats : Ed Davey called it "bold" and Caroline Voaden welcomed universal work experience. [Press; the quote may relate to the interim report, UNVERIFIED] Think tanks - Resolution Foundation (Ruth Curtice, 17 Nov) [P]: right scale of ambition. UK 15-24 NEET 13.6% in 2025, against 4.8% in the Netherlands. Its concerns: the under-25 rate of under £80 a week (20% below the 25+ rate) is inadequate. The reform creates losers among people unable to work. Most young PIP recipients (almost two thirds) are already in work or education, so PIP reform should not be designed around NEETs. https://www.resolutionfoundation.org/press-releases/government-must-match-milburns-ambition-to-properly-invest-in-young-people/ - IFS : page blocked (403). The search summary says the IFS found the package appropriately system-wide, needing priority at the 2027 Spending Review, and the modelled employment effects hard to judge on the detail published. [Press, UNVERIFIED] https://ifs.org.uk/articles/milburn-review-young-people-and-work-ifs-response - Youth Futures Foundation (Sarah Yong, 17 Nov) [P]: welcomes the 5% "lodestar". Its concerns are local capacity and inactivity that is still rising. https://youthfuturesfoundation.org/news/youth-futures-foundation-responds-to-young-people-and-work-report/ - Bright Blue (Ryan Shorthouse): "bigger and bossier government". Its fix would be cheaper hiring plus tighter access to health benefits. [Press, City AM] - Learning and Work Institute, IPPR, Policy Exchange, CSJ : no response to the final report found on 18 Nov. Before the report, IPPR projected NEETs rising from one in eight to one in six by 2029, and L&W set a goal of under 10% NEET with nobody NEET for more than a year. [Press] Evaluation evidence on earlier schemes - Kickstart (2020-22) , DWP impact assessment, 7 Oct 2024 [P]: 163,000 placements. For every 100 participants, 11 more were in unsubsidised work at 24 months than comparable non-participants, and 3 more were off UC. Return per £1: £1.18 at 2 years and £3.15 at 5 years (all perspectives); £0.27 and £0.49 to the Exchequer. Larger effects for people with weaker prospects. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/kickstart-scheme-a-quantitative-impact-assessment/executive-summary-kickstart-scheme-a-quantitative-impact-assessment . The NAO found weak assurance on additionality and job quality. [Press] - Future Jobs Fund (2009-10) : +11 percentage points in unsubsidised work and -7 points on benefits at 2 years (DWP, Nov 2012, via NIESR). [Press; DWP PDF not opened] Milburn (p.161) states that the FJF and Kickstart effects were "remarkably similar". [P] - Youth Contract wage incentive (2012-14) : only employer surveys found. 19% of employers said they created an extra vacancy (DWP RR828, self-reported). No causal impact estimate found, so UNVERIFIED . 4. France comparison UK instrument Closest French instrument Facts Status --- --- --- --- Opportunity + Support Guarantee; Jobs Guarantee Contrat d'engagement jeune (CEJ) , successor to the Garantie jeunes: intensive support of 6-12 months with a monthly allowance About 700,000 entrants Mar 2022-Jun 2024, 64% via missions locales (IPP). Allowance up to €561.68 a month (value at 1 Apr 2025, IPP). 27,122 entries in Jan 2026 (DARES via DREETS PACA) [Press] / allowance UNVERIFIED Evaluation Garantie jeunes , comité scientifique, interim report Nov 2016 Cohort 1, ~14 months after entry: +6.3 points employment rate for all eligible youth (40.4% vs 34.1% counterfactual), +4.6 points durable employment. For actual beneficiaries: +11.5 points (wave 2). Cohort 2 did not confirm (non-significant). Wave 3: about +9 points, significant only at 10% [P] report p.2-3, ch.4 (copy on banquedesterritoires.fr) Garantie jeunes final report (2018) +7.1 points at about 16 months [Press] UNVERIFIED CEJ evaluation (IPP for DARES, Jan 2026) Employment effect "comparable" to the Garantie jeunes, faster in the short run, slightly lower cost [Press] (Centre Inffo, Banque des territoires); PDF not reachable Duty to participate to 18 (England); "no 16-17 NEET" Obligation de formation 16-18 (loi pour une école de la confiance, 26 July 2019; in force Sept 2020; missions locales check compliance) Cour des comptes RPA 2025: 58% of young people covered were "sans solution effective" in 2023 [Press] education.gouv.fr blocked (403). 58% UNVERIFIED Youth Opportunity Service Missions locales and France Travail Context only Employer hiring payment, apprenticeship £2,500 Aide à l'embauche d'apprentis , décret n° 2026-168 of 6 Mar 2026 (contracts 8 Mar-31 Dec 2026) up to €5,000 (levels 3-4) for firms under 250 staff; lower for higher levels and for large firms (€750-2,000) [Press] UNVERIFIED (sources disagree on levels 5-7) AI Youth Observatory Observatoire France Travail , first study 17 Nov 2026 16,000+ employers surveyed (BMO 2026 AI module). 38% use or test AI; 6% think AI could compete with humans in their main occupation within 5 years; 70% of AI users expect generative-AI skills, but 22% have trained staff. Nothing on young people or entry-level jobs [P] https://www.francetravail.org/accueil/actualites/2026/l-observatoire-france-travail-anticiper-l-avenir-du-travail-pour-mieux-agir.html?type=article Separate Observatoire de l'impact de l'IA sur le travail (DARES), announced Sept 2026 [Press] Do not confuse the two French NEET figures - 15-29: 13.3% in Q3 2026, stable on the quarter and +0.4 point on the year. Youth unemployment for 15-24s is 21.0% (Insee, Informations rapides n° 270, 10 Nov 2026). [P] https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/9118603 - 15-24: 10.5% in 2023, against 9.2% for the EU. For 25-29s it is 16.3% (EU 15.1%) (Insee, Formations et emploi, 12 Feb 2025). [P] https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/8305542?sommaire=8306008 - EU 15-29: 11.0% in 2025; Netherlands 5.3% (Eurostat, 28 May 2026). [P] - Comparability warning. UK ONS uses ages 16-24 (13.0%) and France reports 15-29 (13.3%). On the same 15-24 band, the UK (13.6%, OECD 2025) is well above France (10.5%, 2023). Do not put 13.0% and 13.3% side by side as if they were comparable. Read-across. Milburn converges on what France already has in law: a guarantee with an allowance (CEJ), a duty to 18, and a local youth network. What France lacks, and what Milburn proposes: (a) a guaranteed paid job as a backstop; (b) a school-level destination measure and a work-readiness standard, both inspected; (c) a body tracking entry-level jobs under AI by sector and place; (d) mandatory early-warning (RONI) tools in school.

titre: Are young master's graduates doing worse than bachelor's graduates? US evidence and the French case
texte: Research note for the GT Éducation, 18 November 2026. Question: is the master's degree losing value for young graduates relative to the bachelor's (2023-2026), and what does that mean for France, where 29.1 % of 25-34 year olds hold at least a master's level degree, against 19.8 % in the UK, 16.7 % in Germany and 13 % in the US (OECD, cited by J.-C. Simon, Les Echos, 9 Nov 2026; used as given, see research/article-smicardisation-formation-2026-11.md ). Bottom line. Levanon's claim is about master's holders compared with their own past , not with bachelor's holders. In the US, young master's holders still have lower unemployment than bachelor's-only holders, but the gap closed in 2025. In France, bac+5 graduates still clearly outperform bac+3/4 on employment, unemployment, pay and stable jobs at three years (Céreq, Génération 2021). The French weak points are elsewhere: the 2024-2025 fall in junior cadre hiring, and a high and rising share of university master's graduates who are not cadres. 1. What it shows Verified (primary source read) 1. Levanon: master's unemployment is high for master's holders, not higher than for bachelor's holders. Gad Levanon (Burning Glass Institute), "The Masters Degree Problem", Labor Matters , 13 April 2026: unemployment of master's holders (MA, MS, MBA, MEd) under 35 sits at the 77th percentile of its own 2003-2026 history (24-month moving average), against the 22nd percentile for professional and doctorate holders (MD, JD, PhD). The post gives no rates in percent, no bachelor's comparison and no named data source (the NY Post / WSJ coverage says BLS data). Mechanisms he proposes: (a) supply glut, notably online MBAs and data or analytics MS programs; (b) a master's is "a signal rather than a license", and "signals lose value when everyone has one"; (c) sector exposure, as technology-driven weakness in finance, consulting and tech hits master's holders, who are concentrated there. https://gadlevanon.substack.com/p/the-masters-degree-problem . The LinkedIn version (title "Think young college grads have it bad? Look at those with master's degrees") returned HTTP 403 and was not read ; I assume, without being able to verify, that it is the same analysis. 2. US, ages 25-34, CPS (BLS via FRED, not seasonally adjusted, annual averages computed by me). Unemployment of master's holders: 1.9 % in 2022, 2.1 % in 2023, 2.5 % in 2024, 3.2 % in 2025, 2.9 % in Jan-Oct 2026. Bachelor's-only: 2.5 %, 2.8 %, 3.1 %, 3.3 %, 3.5 %. Master's holders are still below bachelor's holders every year; the gap fell from 0.8 point in 2023 to 0.1 point in 2025, then reopened to 0.6 point in 2026. Over Nov 2025-Oct 2026: 3.0 % against 3.4 %. Series CGMD2534 and CGBD2534, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CGMD2534 . Monthly values are noisy (for example 1.9 % against 3.3 % in October 2026). 3. US recent graduates in general (NY Fed, 22-27, bachelor's or higher). Unemployment 5.2 % in 2026 Q3, its lowest in more than a year; underemployment 42.5 %, up in the quarter. The NY Fed series does not split master's from bachelor's. https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/college-labor-market 4. France, three years after leaving education (Céreq, Génération 2021, surveyed 2024). Master's (university, level 7) against bac+3/4: employment 87 % vs 78 % , unemployment 9 % vs 13 % , median first income 1,810 € vs 1,530 € net per month, stable jobs (CDI, civil servant, self-employed) 71 % vs 67 % . Engineering and business schools: 90 % employment, 7 % unemployment, 2,130 €. Overall the hierarchy by diploma level holds, and the Céreq writes that "l'hypothèse d'une inflation des diplômes ... n'est donc pas privilégiée". But on déclassement (normative: a bac+5 is déclassé if not cadre or business owner; a bac+3/4 if not cadre or profession intermédiaire), "la situation relative des diplômés de master ... est souvent moins favorable que celle des diplômés de bac+3/4 ou même de niveau bac". Overall déclassement rose from 26 % (Génération 2004) to 32 % (Génération 2021), mostly among short-cycle tertiary graduates; it has been falling for a decade among bac+5 and above. Ilardi, Lercari, Merlin, Céreq Bref 487-488, July 2026, https://www.cereq.fr/sites/default/files/2026-07/Bref 487-488 OK.pdf 5. France, 12 months after graduating (MESR-SIES, InserSup, graduates under 30 not continuing studies). Salaried employment in France at 12 months, 2024 graduates: licence professionnelle 79.8 %, master (excluding teaching) 70.4 %, licence générale 61.9 % ; master down 0.8 point on 2023. Net monthly full-time-equivalent pay of 2022 graduates (interquartile range): master 1,850 to 2,610 €, licence pro 1,710 to 2,170 €, licence générale 1,530 to 1,950 €. Note Flash SIES n° 33, December 2025, https://www.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2025-12/nf-sies-2025-33--38991.pdf . Caveat: the vocational licence pro beats the master on early salaried employment, but not on pay; the comparison excludes self-employment and work abroad. 6. France, the 2024-2025 shock to bac+5 hiring (Apec). Salaried employment at 12 months of bac+5 graduates fell from 74 % (class of 2022) to 72 % (class of 2023) ; business schools 66 % (-4 points), IT 75 % (-4), engineers 77 %, letters-languages-arts 59 %. Junior cadre hiring fell 19 % in 2024 and was forecast to fall 16 % in 2025, driven by IT services, engineering-R&D, legal, accounting and consulting services. 84 % of the 2024 class found the job search difficult (61 % for 2022); 24 % call their job "alimentaire" (+7 points). Apec attributes the fall to the investment slump and political uncertainty, not to AI . Apec, "Jeunes diplômé.es d'un Bac +5", November 2025 (InserSup, plus a survey of 1,595 graduates, June 2025), https://www.banquedesterritoires.fr/sites/default/files/2025-11/Apec-Jeunes-diplom%C3%A9s-Bac%2B5-une-insertion-plus-difficile.pdf UNVERIFIED (secondary sources, or primary not read) 7. Apec barometer Q1 2026: about 70 % of bac+5 graduates in employment about 12 months after graduating (June 2025); seen only as a truncated search snippet. https://corporate.apec.fr/files/live/sites/corporate/files/Nos%20etudes/PDF/Barometre%20Apec%20T1%202026.pdf 8. Céreq (Génération 2017, via Le Monde, January 2024): the cadre share among master's graduates at three years fell from 56 % (Génération 1998) to 49 % (Génération 2017) ; bac+5 unemployment rose from 5 % to 9 %. Céreq (Génération 2017, via L'Express Éducation): university master's graduates were 85 % employed at three years, 63 % cadres in October 2020, against 75 % for other bac+5 (schools). https://lexpress-education.com/articles/les-diplomes-de-master-universitaire-ont-ils-tous-les-memes-debuts-de-vie-active/ 9. US employers: more than 40 % plan to hire no master's holders in 2026, against 28.6 % in 2025 (Drexel LeBow survey, via NY Post / AOL, 21 May 2026); US master's programs grew 69 % between 2005 and 2021 (same article). https://www.aol.com/articles/master-degrees-yielding-fewest-jobs-194217778.html 10. Mon Master 2025: about 250,400 candidates confirmed at least one wish (+10 % on 2024), 17.3 applications per place against 12.7 in 2023; in 2024, 85.7 % of 191,700 eligible candidates received an offer (meilleurs-masters.com, letudiant.fr; ministry page blocked, HTTP 403). Master's enrolments at university rose 2.5 % (+14,900) in 2024-2025 (SIES, via search snippet), which implies about 610,000 students (my calculation, à vérifier). 11. OECD Education at a Glance 2025: OECD-wide, a master's or doctorate earns 83 % more than upper secondary, against 39 % for a bachelor's (25-64, full-time). France-specific 2025 figures not found (OECD pages blocked); EAG 2022 gave France 42 % (bachelor's) and 81 % (master's), against OECD 44 % and 88 %. Check Table A4.1 of EAG 2025. Not found, to search if needed: the Céreq Génération 2021 subjective sur-qualification measure by level; Insee or Cour des comptes data on master's graduates paid near the SMIC; a DARES/France Stratégie update on surqualification after 2023. 2. How it applies to France The French version of the argument (Simon: "smicardisation et surqualification", a "machine à frustration") runs: France produces twice the US share of master's holders, into an economy whose wage structure is compressed towards the SMIC (Rexecode: +8 points in 30 years of private employees paid below 80 % of the average wage), so many master's holders end up in jobs below their expectations. What holds. - The master's is less often a ticket to cadre status: only about half of university master's graduates start as cadres, and their normative déclassement compares badly with bac+3/4 (Céreq). Levanon's "signal, not license" point fits the French university master's well, as against engineering and business schools. - France had its own 2024-2025 shock, concentrated in the same sectors Levanon names (IT, consulting, finance and accounting services): junior cadre hiring -19 % then -16 %, business-school graduates down 4 points (Apec). - The vocational licence pro does better than the master on early salaried employment (79.8 % vs 70.4 % at 12 months), which supports the case for shorter, applied tracks. What does not hold. - The French bac+5 still clearly outperforms the bac+3/4 on every Céreq indicator at three years: +9 points of employment, -4 points of unemployment, +280 € of median first income. The Céreq explicitly rejects diploma inflation for bac+5 and finds déclassement falling at that level. - Even in the US, young master's holders are not doing worse than bachelor's holders in levels; they are doing worse than they used to. - The master's median first income (1,810 €) is well above the SMIC; the smicardisation problem bites hardest on non-graduates (whose median first income is below one full-time SMIC, Céreq) and on short-cycle graduates, whose déclassement rose most. Honest framing for the notes: the problem is not "too many masters" in general, but too many master's programs that do not lead to cadre jobs, and too little information about which ones do. That supports note 3's proposal to publish outcomes by programme, rather than a call to cut master's places. 3. Use in the notes 1. notes/note3-orienter.md , section 4 « Après le bac : une information claire face à l'IA », first bullet « Les jeunes sont déjà touchés », add at the end: « Le master reste un bon investissement : trois ans après la sortie, 87 % des diplômés de master sont en emploi, contre 78 % des bac+3/4 (Céreq, Génération 2021). Mais il ne garantit plus un poste de cadre, et le résultat varie fortement d'un master à l'autre. » 2. notes/note3-orienter.md , section 4, second bullet « Un indice public dans Parcoursup », add: « L'affichage doit aussi couvrir Mon Master : taux d'emploi, salaire et part de cadres, formation par formation. Un an après le diplôme, 70,4 % des diplômés de master sont salariés en France, contre 79,8 % des licences professionnelles (SIES, 2025). » 3. notes/ia-jeunes-emploi/2026-11-16-note-ia-jeunes-emploi-orientation.md , « Le constat, en chiffres », new bullet after the second one: « Les bac+5 sont touchés aussi : les recrutements de cadres débutants ont chuté de 19 % en 2024, surtout dans l'informatique, l'ingénierie et le conseil, et 72 % des bac+5 de 2023 étaient salariés un an après, contre 74 % pour la promotion précédente (Apec, 2025). » « La France compte plus de diplômés de master que ses voisins : 29,1 % des 25-34 ans, contre 19,8 % au Royaume-Uni et 16,7 % en Allemagne (OCDE). Le master protège encore du chômage, mais seuls les métiers qui exigent vraiment ce diplôme le récompensent. » (The second sentence paraphrases Levanon's "signal, not license"; it is an interpretation, not a French figure. Keep it as a line for the candidate, or add « à vérifier » if used in the constat.) 5. Same note, « Les conditions », bullet « Une orientation qui suit le marché du travail », add: « Étendre cet affichage aux masters sur Mon Master, où les candidatures par place sont passées de 12,7 en 2023 à 17,3 en 2025 (chiffres à vérifier). » Full URLs are given inline above.

titre: Does a young hire need a master's? Evidence on the master as a filter
texte: GT Éducation fact sheet, 18 November 2026. Companion to 2026-11-18-masters-job-market.md (Céreq, Apec, InserSup, Levanon: not repeated here). Labels: [P] primary source read. SECONDARY = press, think tank or search snippet only. UNVERIFIED = not confirmed. NOT FOUND = searched, nothing usable. 1. Degree inflation and the requirement gap (US, UK) - SECONDARY. Fuller and Raman, Dismissed by Degrees (HBS, Accenture, Grads of Life, Oct 2017): 26 million 2015 postings plus a survey of 600 business and HR leaders. 67 % of production supervisor postings asked for a bachelor's degree, against 16 % of people already in the job; 6.2 million middle-skill jobs "at risk of degree inflation". HBS PDF returned 404: https://www.hbs.edu/managing-the-future-of-work/Documents/dismissed-by-degrees.pdf ; summary https://pw.hks.harvard.edu/post/dismissed-by-degrees - SECONDARY. Burning Glass Institute and HBS, The Emerging Degree Reset (Feb 2022, 51 million postings, 2017 vs 2019-Mar 2021): degree requirements fell materially in 46 % of middle-skill and 31 % of high-skill occupations; production supervisor postings asking for a BA fell to 33 % by 2020. https://www.bollettinoadapt.it/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/TheEmergingDegreeReset22.02Final.pdf - Outcomes are weak. Sigelman, Fuller, Martin, Skills-Based Hiring: The Long Road from Pronouncements to Practice (BGI and HBS, Feb 2024; authors and date [P], figures SECONDARY ): removing a degree requirement raised non-degree hiring in those roles by 3.5 points on average, about 97,000 extra hires a year out of 77 million (fewer than 1 in 700); most of the change came from 37 % of firms; at "leader" firms non-degree hires had retention 10 points higher than graduates. https://burningglassinstitute.org/research/skills-based-hiring-2024 (PDF download blocked) - US states. [P] National Governors Association, 11 Feb 2025: "over half of U.S. state governments" have skills-based hiring policies, including dropping degree requirements; non-degree postings grew faster in those states (postings, not hires). https://www.nga.org/news/press-releases/new-report-growing-number-of-states-drop-degree-requirements/ . Exact count SECONDARY : 20 to 27 states depending on definition (14 by executive order, Oct 2024). Federal government: not checked. - UK. [P] Indeed Hiring Lab (L. Feist, 29 Aug 2024): only 14 % of UK postings mention any education requirement (about 50 % in the US); 4.6 % require a bachelor's or higher, under 1 % a master's or doctorate; 52 % of sectors ask for degrees less than six years earlier. https://hiringlab.indeed.com/uk/blog/2024/08/29/job-postings-formal-education-requirements/ . Civil Service Fast Stream still asks for a 2:2 but counts degree apprenticeships ( SECONDARY , gov.uk page 403). Milburn final report (17 Nov 2026) [P, via research/12-milburn-review/ ]: apprenticeships as top skills priority, about 270,000 under-25 starts a year by 2036; 11 % of Civil Service entry staff aged 16-24 by 2032. NOT FOUND : any Milburn recommendation to drop degree requirements. 2. France: what junior jobs ask for, and over-qualification - NOT FOUND: a study of the share of French junior ("jeune diplômé", "débutant") offers requiring bac+5 or prior experience (Apec, France Travail, Indeed, HelloWork). Apec defines "débutant" as under one year of experience. Lack of experience is the top obstacle cited by bac+5 graduates ( 79 % , Apec Nov 2025, SECONDARY , apec.fr 403). - [P, CSO Ireland reproducing OECD PIAAC 2023, Table 3.1; workers 25-65, not self-employed]: France 19 % over-qualified against OECD 23 % ; under-qualified 12 % vs 9 %; well matched 69 % vs 67 %. Over-skilled 25 % vs 26 %. France is less over-qualified than average. https://www.cso.ie/en/releasesandpublications/ep/p-piaac/programmefortheinternationalassessmentofadultcompetenciespiaac2023-skillsuseandsocialoutcomes/skillsmismatch - Céreq Génération 2021 (in companion file): normative déclassement 32 % overall, falling for bac+5; but master's graduates compare badly with bac+3/4 on it. 3. Public service - [P] Teacher recruitment (devenirenseignant.gouv.fr): since the 2026 session CRPE, Capes, Capeps, CPE, Capet and CAPLP are open from the third year of licence. Laureates then do a two-year master: M1 as élève fonctionnaire, about 1,400 € net/month ; M2 as fonctionnaire stagiaire, about 1,800 € , half-time in class; 4-year service commitment. https://www.devenirenseignant.gouv.fr/reforme-du-recrutement-et-de-la-formation-initiale-des-professeurs-mieux-former-pour-mieux-faire-1516 . Decree of 19 April 2025 (n° 2025-352?) UNVERIFIED . Note: the master is kept, but selection moves to bac+3 and the master becomes paid training. - Attaché d'administration (IRA, first category A grade): external concours requires a licence (bac+3) ( SECONDARY , emploipublic.fr). "More than 80 % of external laureates hold a master or grande école diploma" ( UNVERIFIED , carrieres-publiques.com). - [P] Mon Master 2025 (SIES Note Flash 32, Dec 2025): 258,300 candidates (+10 %), 68 % received an offer (71 % in 2024), 56 % accepted one. By origin: L3 générale 82 % , BUT 57 %, licence pro 48 % . https://www.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2025-12/nf-sies-2025-32-38737.pdf 4. Signalling - [P, abstract] Jaeger and Page, "Degrees Matter", Review of Economics and Statistics 78(4), 1996: using actual degree receipt (CPS 1991-92) rather than years of schooling substantially raises the estimated diploma ("sheepskin") effects for high school and college. https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:tpr:restat:v:78:y:1996:i:4:p:733-40 . Magnitudes (+24.5 % college) SECONDARY . Hungerford and Solon (1987, ReStat ): citation only, content UNVERIFIED . - [P] French quasi-sheepskin evidence. Insee Première n° 2109 (E. Pouliquen, June 2026), cohort entering 6e in 2007, aged 26-27 in 2023, comparing graduates with those who reached the final year and failed or left. Master: employment 90 % vs 87 % ( not significant ); net pay 2,240 € vs 2,130 €, +4 % after controls; cadre 56 % vs 42 %, +15 points after controls (social origin, sex, past achievement). Licence: cadre or profession intermédiaire +17 points. So the master certificate barely changes pay or employment, but strongly gates access to cadre jobs. https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/9003866 - Caveat: this is consistent with signalling or credential rules, but final-year learning and residual selection are not excluded. NOT FOUND : a French estimate of the master vs licence return net of selection. 5. Social unfairness - [P] RERS 2025, table 7.16-3 (French students at universities, 2024-2025, unknown origin excluded): children of cadres 31.1 % in licence, 42.1 % in master , 41.6 % in doctorate; children of ouvriers 10.1 %, 6.3 % , 3.9 %; employés 20.8 %, 14.3 %, 10.0 %. All students: 36 % cadres, 9 % ouvriers. https://www.education.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2025-07/rers2025-chapitre-7-441732.pdf - NOT FOUND: Mon Master offer rates by bursary status or social origin (2024 and 2025 notes give none). "Nearly one in three" 2023 registrants were boursiers ( SECONDARY , letudiant.fr). - SIES (Nov 2025): licence in 3-4 years for 48.8 % of very favoured vs 32 % of less favoured students ( SECONDARY , snippet). 6. Cost - [P] RERS 2025, table 10.05-2 (2023, provisional, 2023 prices): 12,250 € per university student per year ; all higher education 13,060 €; STS 16,730 €; CPGE 18,560 €. Two master's years ≈ 24,500 € of spending (my calculation; master-specific cost not published). https://www.education.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/document/rers-2025-chapitre-10-522891.pdf - Living costs ( SECONDARY ): UNEF Aug 2025, about 1,226 €/month (≈ 29,400 € over 24 months, my calculation); FAGE 2025, 3,227 € start-of-year cost for a non-bursary licence student; fees 178 € (licence) vs 254 € (master). - Forgone earnings (my calculation, crude): 24 months at the Céreq bac+3/4 median first income (1,530 € net) ≈ 36,700 €, less if unemployed. The master's +280 €/month median premium (1,810 € vs 1,530 €) takes about 11 years to repay that, ignoring pay growth and the master's better employment rate. 7. Employer surveys - [P] Lumina Foundation and Gallup, 2,500 US hiring decision-makers, 5-18 Aug 2026 (opt-in, unweighted): 80 % prefer a candidate with a degree (31 % strongly), and the preference holds even where the role does not require one. https://news.gallup.com/poll/715601/employers-confidence-higher-education-undaunted.aspx - SECONDARY: Cengage 2023, 50 % of 1,000 US employers require a degree for entry jobs (62 % in 2022); Dismissed by Degrees survey: degree holders cost 11-30 % more without matching productivity ( UNVERIFIED ). - NOT FOUND: any French survey (public or private employers) on whether entry jobs truly need the degree level demanded. The proposed poll would fill a real gap. Verdict per claim Claim Verdict Why --- --- --- (a) Gap between required and needed level Partly Strong US evidence (67 % vs 16 %); in France only indirect (IRA licence rule vs mostly-master laureates, unverified); no French ad study (b) Master mainly a filter/signal Partly Insee: certificate adds +15 points cadre access but only +4 % pay; yet master still beats bac+3/4 on jobs and pay; human capital not ruled out (c) Unfair to poorer students Supported (access) Cadres 31 % → 42 %, ouvriers 10 % → 6 %; selection by bursary status not measured (d) Costly for young people Supported ≈ 29,000 € living costs + forgone earnings, ≈ 24,500 € public money; partly repaid by the premium (e) Wastes talent Weak / contrary France 19 % over-qualified vs OECD 23 %; bac+5 déclassement falling; only Céreq's master vs bac+3/4 comparison and Apec "jobs alimentaires" support it Five French sentences for a campaign note 1. « À l'université, les enfants de cadres représentent 31 % des étudiants de licence mais 42 % des étudiants de master ; les enfants d'ouvriers passent de 10 % à 6 % (RERS 2025, année 2024-2025). » 2. « Une année d'université coûte 12 250 euros par étudiant (RERS 2025) : deux ans de master, c'est environ 24 500 euros d'argent public, plus environ 1 200 euros par mois de frais de vie pour l'étudiant (UNEF 2025, à vérifier). » 3. « L'État a montré la voie : depuis 2026, on passe le concours de professeur dès la licence, puis le master est payé environ 1 400 puis 1 800 euros nets par mois (ministère de l'Éducation nationale). » 4. « Le diplôme de master ouvre surtout une porte : à 26-27 ans, l'obtenir plutôt qu'échouer en dernière année augmente de 15 points la probabilité d'être cadre, mais le salaire de 4 % seulement (Insee, juin 2026). » 5. « Aux États-Unis, 67 % des offres de chef d'équipe de production exigeaient une licence, alors que 16 % des titulaires du poste en avaient une (Harvard Business School, 2017, à vérifier) ; en France, personne n'a mesuré cet écart, d'où notre consultation des employeurs. »

titre: Do French firms use the master's as a filter? And how do we get young people into work faster?
texte: GT Éducation research note, 18 November 2026. Companions: 2026-11-18-masters-job-market.md (Céreq, Apec, InserSup, Levanon) and 2026-11-18-master-as-filter-evidence.md (US/UK degree inflation, PIAAC, teacher concours at L3). Neither is repeated here. Milburn details come from research/12-milburn-review/2026-11-18-milburn-review.md . Labels: VERIFIED = primary source read this session. SECONDARY = press, think tank, search snippet, or a primary source cited by another paper. UNVERIFIED = not confirmed. NOT FOUND = searched, nothing usable. 1. Executive summary 1. Verdict: moderate, mostly indirect evidence. French data show the diploma works as a first-stage screen on CVs, not as the reason a candidate is finally chosen. No French study measures the share of junior offers that demand a bac+5 the job does not need. 2. Best French evidence (Dares, Ofer 2016): the diploma is the final selection criterion in only 11 % of hires ( 22 % for cadres), but the survey reports it "peut servir de filtre pour trier les candidats". 73 % of recruiters say they could have hired someone less qualified but more experienced. 3. Comparative evidence: in a nine-country recruiter experiment, French and German recruiters preferred master's graduates for junior posts; UK recruiters preferred bachelor's graduates (SECONDARY). EY-Parthenon says it hires "quasi exclusivement des masters" in France but opens UK and Luxembourg offices to bachelors (SECONDARY). 4. Against the filter story: French job ads ask for fewer diplomas over time (Indeed: no diploma stated in 61.7 % of 2024 ads, up from 53.1 % in 2017), 29 % of private-sector cadres hold less than bac+3, and bac+5 still pays more than bac+3/4 (Céreq). 5. Reading: the filter works through the candidate pool (79 % of applicants to Apec cadre offers hold bac+5), not through written requirements. Students take a master's because everyone else does, a classic signalling race. 6. Most promising levers: professionalised licence with alternance (licence pro beats master on early employment), State as exemplary employer, outcome data per programme, and a recurring employer question "un diplômé moins élevé aurait-il convenu ?" that Ofer already asked once. 7. Generic hiring subsidies are weak: the 2020-21 AEJ raised youth hiring by about 8 % but cost more than 900 M€ with no clear effect on total youth employment. 8. Biggest gaps: a French job-ad study of junior bac+5 requirements, and any French evaluation of MRS or skills-based hiring outcomes. 2. Part 1: Evidence that French firms use bac+5 as a selection device 2.1 Job ads - VERIFIED. French ads require fewer diplomas, not more. Indeed Hiring Lab France (Lisa Feist, 12 Nov 2024), all French Indeed postings, Jan-Sep each year: postings with no diploma requirement rose from 53.1 % (2017) to 61.7 % (2024) ; postings asking at least a licence fell from 16.4 % to 14.5 % . The licence requirement fell in 83 % of job families. Largest falls: insurance −12.7 points, marketing −6.9, HR −6.5, software development −5.9. Increases in regulated health jobs (pharmacy +9.1, nursing +7.1). Bac+5 not reported separately. https://hiringlab.indeed.com/fr/blog/2024/11/12/le-diplome-est-de-moins-en-moins-important-sur-le-marche-du-travail-en-france/ - VERIFIED. Apec cadre offers, 2024. 30 % of cadre offers on apec.fr are open to young graduates (less than one year of experience). 79 % of candidates to Apec cadre offers hold bac+5 or more. Among private-sector cadres in employment, 71 % hold bac+3 or more (Insee Enquêtes Emploi 2023-2024, cited by Apec), so 29 % hold less. Apec, Métiers verts et emploi cadre , Dec 2025, p. 3-4. https://corporate.apec.fr/files/live/sites/corporate/files/Nos%20etudes/PDF/metiers%20verts%20et%20emploi%20cadre%202025.pdf . (A search snippet claimed "54 % of private-sector cadres hold bac+5": not found in the text; do not use.) - NOT FOUND. Share of "jeune diplômé" or "débutant accepté" offers requiring bac+5 (Apec, France Travail, HelloWork, Jobteaser, Welcome to the Jungle), and any French "diploma required vs diploma held" comparison by occupation. The companion file reached the same result. - Reading. The French filter is not written in ads. It operates through who applies and who gets shortlisted: when 79 % of applicants hold bac+5, a recruiter can screen on it without stating it. 2.2 Recruiter practice and surveys - VERIFIED. Diploma used to sort, rarely to choose. Pôle emploi, Éclairages et synthèses n° 43, March 2018, on Dares Ofer 2016 (establishments that recruited Sept-Nov 2015). In a CV, 74 % of employers look first at experience in the trade and 57 % at behavioural skills; 40 % look first at diplomas, more in large establishments. The diploma is cited as a reason for the final choice in 11 % of hires: 22 % for cadres, 17 % for professions intermédiaires, 3 % for low-skilled workers. Quote: the diploma "peut servir de filtre pour trier les candidats dans un premier temps"; 60 % of employers call it important for cadre and intermediate posts. https://www.francetravail.org/files/live/sites/peorg/files/documents/Statistiques-et-analyses/E%26S/ES 43 comment les employeurs selectionent les candidats qu'ils retiennent dans leur recrutement.pdf - VERIFIED. Recruiters admit a less qualified hire would have done. Lhommeau and Rémy, Économie et Statistique n° 534-35, 2022, Ofer 2016, Table 4: 35 % of recruiters had no diploma expectation; 73 % say they "aurai[en]t pu embaucher quelqu'un de moins diplômé mais de plus expérimenté" ( 71 % in technical occupations, the class where 64 % of hires hold bac+2 or more). Caveat: all hires, not cadres débutants; the trade-off is diploma against experience, which young graduates lack. https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/fichier/6530515/04 ES534-35 Lhommeau-Remy FR.pdf - SECONDARY. Dares Analyses n° 10, Feb 2022, "Comment les employeurs recrutent-ils un jeune candidat ?" (Ofer 2016): for juniors, dynamism, presentation and being operational come first; "plus le niveau d'études est élevé, plus le diplôme est déterminant". Dares site blocked by captcha; via Lefebvre Dalloz and BnF notice. https://dares.travail-emploi.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/8f21e540868fb8b28f62420de04cfc74/DA recrutement jeunes.pdf - SECONDARY. Céreq, upgrading of intermediate jobs. Cadet, Delanoë, Guitton, Céreq Bref n° 397, 2020: entry into professions intermédiaires (historically bac+2) is now mostly at bac+3; firms use the diploma as a guarantee of general capacities and teach job skills in-house; share of higher-education graduates in these jobs 48.5 % in 2017. Read via an AEF summary only (Céreq and HAL blocked). https://halshs.archives-ouvertes.fr/halshs-03045526v1/file/cadet bref397 2020.pdf - SECONDARY. School name. L'Etudiant poll of 200 recruiters (undated): only 4 % attach much importance to the school or university name. https://www.letudiant.fr/jobsstages/lettres-de-motivation 1/sondage-exclusif-ce-que-les-recruteurs-regardent-le-plus-sur-les-cv-17376.html . No source found for published "école cible" lists ( NOT FOUND ). - NOT FOUND. An Ofer wave after 2016; Institut Montaigne, CAE or France Stratégie notes specifically on bac+5 as a hiring filter. 2.3 Academic evidence on signalling and credentialism - SECONDARY. France prefers masters, the UK bachelors. Humburg and van der Velden, "Skills and the graduate recruitment process", Economics of Education Review 49 (2015): vignette experiments with recruiters in nine European countries for a typical junior graduate post. On average bachelor's and master's graduates were treated equally, but "recruiters in the UK [had] a preference for bachelor graduates and recruiters in several other countries, such as France and Germany, ... for master graduates". Quoted from Verhaest et al. (below); original not read (PDF download failed). https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:eee:ecoedu:v:49:y:2015:i:c:p:24-41 - VERIFIED (Belgium, not France). Employers reward over-qualification. Verhaest, Bogaert, Dereymaeker, Mestdagh, Baert, "Do employers prefer overqualified graduates? A field experiment", Industrial Relations , 2018: paired fictitious applications to real Belgian vacancies requiring a bachelor's. Master's applicants were 19 % more likely to be invited to interview and 11 % more likely to get any positive reply, more so in shortage occupations. This is the mechanism behind a degree race: when a master's beats a bachelor's for bachelor-level jobs, students rationally continue. https://lirias.kuleuven.be/retrieve/c0c04b1f-6299-4b9f-9223-1063f8187b45 - SECONDARY. Crowding-out down the ladder. Insee ( Le non-emploi des peu ou pas diplômés en France et en Europe : un effet classement du diplôme , 2020): a person's rank in the diploma distribution predicts non-employment; through the déclassement of graduates, the least qualified were partly pushed out of work. Snippet only. https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/4501168 - VERIFIED (bibliographic) / SECONDARY (content). Marie Duru-Bellat, L'inflation scolaire. Les désillusions de la méritocratie , Seuil, La République des idées, 2006: argues accumulated credentials lose value as everyone acquires them. https://www.mollat.com/livres/57175/marie-duru-bellat-l-inflation-scolaire-les-desillusions-de-la-meritocratie - NOT FOUND. A French correspondence test comparing bac+3 and bac+5 (or university and grande école) applicants for the same junior job. The TEPP/ONDES "MASTER" tests concern access to master's programmes, not to jobs. 2.4 Sector cases - SECONDARY. Strategy consulting. Consultor, 15 Dec 2025, reporting Jérôme Fabry (partner, EY-Parthenon): "en France, EY-Parthenon recrute quasi exclusivement des masters"; the opening of UK and Luxembourg offices "aux « bachelors » ou BBA" shows "qu'il ne s'agit pas d'une contrainte métier, mais d'un choix culturel". https://www.consultor.fr/articles/vers-la-fin-de-la-prime-au-bac-5-y-compris-dans-le-conseil-en-strategie - SECONDARY. Audit (Big Four France). Junior ads from KPMG and PwC France ask for bac+5 (business school, engineering school or university); bac+3 entry exists mainly as alternance (DCG holders going on to DSCG). Aggregator ads and older recruitment brochures, not a study. https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/pdf/2016/06/fr-recrutement-plaquette.pdf - SECONDARY. Public sector. The external concours for attaché d'administration de l'État (first category A grade) requires a licence (level 6), not a master's (digiSchool, IRA brochures). https://www.digischool.fr/articles/concours/concours-attache-administration-etat-2027/ . Teacher concours moved to L3 in 2026: see companion file. - SECONDARY. Recruitment without CV or diploma. France Travail's MRS (méthode de recrutement par simulation) excludes CV, diploma and experience; candidates who pass job simulations go to interview. Evidence is testimony only (e.g. candidate pools "multipliés par trois, voire quatre"). The one evaluation found (2010) could not be opened. Used mostly for volume and shortage jobs, not cadre posts. https://www.francetravail.fr/employeur/vos-recrutements/selectionnez-des-candidats/la-methode-de-recrutement-par-si.html - NOT FOUND. Sourced, quantified French corporate programmes hiring licence holders into roles usually given to bac+5 (La Poste, Orange, L'Oréal, Accor were searched; nothing usable). 2.5 Counter-evidence - VERIFIED (companion file). Bac+5 still beats bac+3/4 three years out: employment 87 % vs 78 %, median first pay 1,810 € vs 1,530 € (Céreq Génération 2021). Céreq rejects the diploma-inflation hypothesis at bac+5. - UNVERIFIED (not checked this session). Regulated professions (medicine, pharmacy, law via the bar school, chartered accountancy) and the engineering title genuinely require bac+5 or more. - Interpretation. A real premium is compatible with a filter: if firms screen on bac+5, holders earn more whether or not the job needs it. Only a test of the same job filled at bac+3 vs bac+5 would separate the two, and none exists for France. 3. Part 2: Solutions to speed up entry into work What Precedent and evidence Cost Who French one-liner --- --- --- --- --- --- 1 Professionalised licence : compulsory long internship or alternance in L3; more licence pro and BUT places Salaried employment at 18 months, 2022 graduates: licence pro 81.3 % , master (non-teaching) 73.4 % , licence générale 55.3 % ; CDI 75.7 % vs 64.9 % (Insee, Formations et emploi 2025, InserSup; VERIFIED) https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/8305530 . Selection effect not removed. à chiffrer Universities, MESR « Une licence qui mène à un métier, avec un vrai stage ou une alternance en dernière année. » 2 Finish the licence on time : tutoring, accelerated or compensated tracks Only 30.1 % of 2020 bacheliers in L1 got their licence in 3 years, 40.3 % in 3 or 4 years (down 5.4 points on 2019); 14.0 % for bac techno, 6.5 % for bac pro (SIES Note Flash n° 29, Nov 2025; VERIFIED) https://www.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2025-11/nf-sies-2025-29-38293.pdf à chiffrer Universities, State « Six étudiants sur dix n'ont pas leur licence en quatre ans : c'est là qu'il faut agir. » 3 Apprenticeship and degree apprenticeships at bac+3 rather than bac+5; target apprenticeship aid on bac+3 England: 60,350 level 6-7 apprenticeship starts in 2024/25, 17.1 % of starts, +20.4 % (DfE, 27 Nov 2025; VERIFIED) https://explore-education-statistics.service.gov.uk/find-statistics/apprenticeships/2024-25 . Germany, Duales Studium: about 3 % of dual graduates unemployed vs 6 % of regular bachelor's graduates at 18 months (Krone et al., Böckler Impuls 2019; SECONDARY, survey, no causal design) https://www.boeckler.de/data/Boeckler Impuls 2019 02 4-5.pdf . France: 61 % of 2024 apprentice entrants prepare a higher-education diploma; bac+5 or more was 21 % of new contracts in 2023 (Dares via regional notes; SECONDARY). Reallocates existing apprenticeship aid; à chiffrer State, employers, CFA « L'alternance dès la licence : un emploi à 21 ans, pas à 23. » 4 Employers drop bac+5 where not needed ; skills-based hiring; MRS for junior roles Recruiters already concede the point: 73 % could have hired someone less qualified (Ofer 2016; VERIFIED). US: dropping a degree requirement raised non-degree hiring by only 3.5 points (companion file; SECONDARY). MRS: no independent recent evaluation ( UNVERIFIED effect). Low for firms Employers, France Travail, Apec « Les entreprises doivent recruter sur les compétences, pas sur le nombre d'années d'études. » 5 State as exemplary employer : catégorie A and contractual posts open at licence; youth-hiring share; procurement clause Attaché concours already at licence (SECONDARY); teachers at L3 from 2026 (companion). Milburn (17 Nov 2026): public employers "open their own doors first", 11 % of Civil Service entry staff aged 16-24 by 2032, youth hiring in public contracts above £5m (research/12, from the report). Low; procurement clause à chiffrer State, local authorities « L'État doit montrer l'exemple : recruter à bac+3 quand le poste le permet. » 6 Public employer survey : "le poste exigeait-il vraiment ce diplôme ?" The question already exists in substance: Ofer 2016 asked whether a less qualified, more experienced person could have been hired (73 % yes; VERIFIED). Ofer has not been rerun since 2016 (no later wave found). BMO (France Travail) does not ask it (UNVERIFIED). Add an item to a new Ofer wave or the Apec recruiter panel, split by cadres débutants. Ofer 2016 had 8,510 respondents; cost à chiffrer Dares, Apec, France Travail « Mesurons enfin combien de postes exigent un bac+5 sans en avoir besoin. » 7 Work first, master later : master in alternance or after 2-3 years of work, VAE, gap year in a job No French effect estimate found ( NOT FOUND ). Teacher reform is a precedent: selection at L3, then a paid master (companion file). Neutral to positive for public finances (shorter full-time study); à chiffrer Universities, employers « Le master après l'emploi, pas à la place de l'emploi. » 8 Targeted hiring incentives (not generic) France AEJ (4,000 € per hire under 26, Aug 2020-May 2021): hires +8 % on average, about 5,000 € of public money per extra 3-month CDD (Martin and Rathelot, CAE Focus 060, May 2021; VERIFIED) https://cae-eco.fr/static/pdf/cae-focus060.pdf . Dares: +7 % in CDI/long CDD (about 60,000 jobs) but no effect on total youth employment; cost over 900 M€ (Dares DE 266, Cour des comptes; SECONDARY). UK Kickstart: +11 per 100 participants in unsubsidised work at 24 months (research/12). Milburn: £3,000 after 6 months NEET, +£2,000 for firms under 50, about £1.1bn a year (research/12). High if generic State « Aider l'embauche des jeunes les plus éloignés, pas subventionner des embauches qui auraient eu lieu. » 9 Outcome information per programme in Parcoursup and Mon Master; per-firm junior hiring commitments Parcoursup 2026 shows InserJeunes/InserSup employment and median pay on programme pages (SECONDARY, Diplomeo); some Mon Master pages hide rates and universities contest InserSup (SECONDARY, France Universités and Résosup, June 2026). Milburn: HE earnings data published prominently; employers asked to name entry-level roles open without experience (research/12; Personnel Today, SECONDARY). Low (data exist) MESR, employers « Chaque master doit afficher combien de ses diplômés trouvent un emploi de cadre, et à quel salaire. » 4. Usable in the campaign note 1. « Le diplôme sert d'abord à trier les CV : il ne décide du choix final que dans 11 % des recrutements, et dans 22 % pour les cadres (Dares, enquête Ofer 2016). » 2. « 73 % des recruteurs reconnaissent qu'ils auraient pu embaucher une personne moins diplômée mais plus expérimentée (Dares, Ofer 2016). » 3. « Au Royaume-Uni, les recruteurs préfèrent un bachelor pour un premier poste ; en France, ils préfèrent un master (Humburg et van der Velden, 2015, à vérifier dans l'original). » 4. « Un an et demi après le diplôme, 81 % des diplômés de licence professionnelle sont salariés, contre 73 % des diplômés de master et 55 % des licences générales (Insee, InserSup, 2025). » 5. « Seuls 30 % des étudiants obtiennent leur licence en trois ans (SIES, 2025) : raccourcir le chemin vers l'emploi commence là. » 6. « La prime à l'embauche des jeunes de 2020 a coûté plus de 900 millions d'euros sans effet net sur l'emploi total des jeunes (Dares, Cour des comptes, à vérifier) : il faut cibler, pas arroser. » Full URLs are given inline above.

titre: Why are French scores falling? Evidence on causes (18 Nov 2026)
texte: GT Éducation. Labels: VERIFIED = primary source read today; SECONDARY = press, search snippet or summary of the primary; UNVERIFIED = not confirmed. Note: education.gouv.fr HTML pages and oecd.org blocked automated access today; DEPP PDFs were read directly. The 18 Nov 2026 DEPP note on the September 2026 tests was not read (page blocked): its figures below are SECONDARY. Corrections after direct reading (Claude, 18 Nov 2026, Chrome; copies in sources/ ). The 18 Nov communiqué and the 2026 DEPP reports (CE1, 6e, 5e, 4e, seconde) were read in full. Use these values instead of the SECONDARY ones in section 1: - CE1 « écrire des mots dictés »: 69.9% in 2026 vs 72.4% in 2025 (-2.5) and -7.2 points since 2019. The 73% for 2023 is only on a chart. - CE1 « lire à voix haute des mots »: 68.3% in 2026 vs 69.9% in 2025 (CE1, not CP; the 74.9% quoted in the press is a subgroup column). - Seconde, weakest groups, vs 2019: maths GT 28.1% vs 19.2%, pro 75.4% vs 66.2% (mean -6 points); French GT 22.1% vs 18.7%, pro 69.8% vs 65.7%. The communiqué compares with 2021 instead. - The 2026 reports give no causal explanation (text searched). The 6e pupil questionnaire (709,000 answers): 73.7% feel ready to succeed, girls 68.4% vs boys 78.6%. Executive summary (ranked by strength of evidence) 1. The fall is international, not French-specific (strong, descriptive). PISA 2025: France's reading score fell 18 points since 2022 after 19 points in 2018-2022; the OECD average fell 14. France tracks the OECD (DEPP NI 26.40). Any explanation must work across countries. 2. Covid explains part of the adolescent fall, not the primary one (moderate). Learning losses persisted (d = -0.14), but are larger in maths than reading. The 2026 CE1/CE2 pupils were not yet at school in 2020. 3. Less reading for pleasure, more screens (moderate, correlational). Ages 16-19: over 5 h of screens a day vs 14 min of reading (CNL 2026). Fits a French-only, adolescent-heavy decline. No causal estimate. 4. Distraction in class (moderate, correlational). PISA 2022: 15 points lower in maths where peers' devices distract. 5. Phone bans (mixed causal evidence). Gains in England 2016 and Norway (girls); null in Sweden 2020, England 2025, US 2026. 6. Lower test effort (weak). French 15-year-olds report the lowest effort in the OECD bar Luxembourg; weakly tied to scores. 7. Mental health (weak link to scores). Trends coincide; no study linking them to French test scores was found. 8. Teacher shortages, hours, composition, test changes (weak or untested). Plausible locally; no direct evidence on the 2026 fall. 1. What the DEPP says - 2026 results (SECONDARY, ministry page via search and economiematin.fr, 18 Nov 2026). Seconde GT: 22.1% in the two weakest French groups vs 12.4% in 2021; maths 28.1% vs 27.6% in 2021. French "taux de maîtrise satisfaisante" -1.6 pts on 2025, in all sectors. CP reading aloud 68.3% vs 74.9% in 2021; CE1 dictation 69.9% vs 73% in 2023; 4e mean score 243 vs 250 in 2023. https://www.education.gouv.fr/evaluations-nationales-de-septembre-2026-506811 ; https://www.economiematin.fr/evaluations-nationales-baisse-francais - No causal attribution. Press coverage reports the DEPP director, Magda Tomasini, only pointing to new collège curricula still being rolled out (SECONDARY, economiematin.fr). The two 2025 notes (NI 26.21, 26.22, June 2026) are purely descriptive: no mention of Covid, screens or reading time (VERIFIED, text searched). - NI 26.22: seconde GT French fell between 2024 and 2025 "et reviennent au niveau de la rentrée 2019"; 20.2% in groups 1-2 (+1.4 pts on 2024); seconde pro French down since 2021; social gaps in French widened by 2 points on 2024 (VERIFIED). https://www.education.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/document/depp-ni-2026-22test-de-positionement-secondepdf-517325.pdf - NI 26.21: 6e still above 2017 in both subjects; 4e French mean down vs 2023 (first year of the 4e test), maths stable (VERIFIED). https://www.cafepedagogique.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/depp-ni-2026-21evals-2dpdf-517319.pdf - The only DEPP causal hint is Covid, and it is cautious. The PISA note says the broad fall since Covid "soulève la question d'éventuels effets durables de cette période" (VERIFIED, NI 26.40, Sept 2026). It links the PISA fall to the seconde test fall since 2021, with a caveat that the two do not measure the same skills. - Cohort arithmetic (our calculation, check with DEPP). In spring 2020, 4e 2026 pupils were in CP, seconde 2026 pupils in CE2, 6e 2026 in moyenne section. CE1/CE2 2026 pupils were not yet at school. Covid school closures therefore cannot explain the 2026 primary falls. They fit the 4e cohort, which lost part of CP, but 6e (stable) undercuts a simple "Covid generation" story. - CSEN / Cnesco: no 2025-26 CSEN or Cnesco statement on causes of the reading fall found (UNVERIFIED gap). The États généraux de la lecture pour la jeunesse (2025) report that parents blame screens and young people cite uninteresting books (SECONDARY, culture.gouv.fr). 2. OECD PISA - PISA 2025 (VERIFIED, DEPP NI 26.40, Sept 2026): https://www.education.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/document/depp-ni-2026-40pisa-mathspdf-520231.pdf - Reading: France 456 vs OECD 461; -18 pts 2022-25, -19 pts 2018-22; OECD -14 pts on 2022. Only 8 OECD countries did not fall. - Below level 2 in reading: 33% (27% in 2022, 21% in 2018, 15% in 2000); OECD 30%. Boys -23 pts, girls -11 in three years; 39% of boys below level 2 vs 26% of girls. - Maths: 458 vs OECD 463; -16 pts on 2022 (OECD about -9), after -21 pts 2018-22. - Screens: 4.9 h/day on devices on school days, of which 3.0 h leisure, vs 3.4 h leisure OECD. High-scoring Estonia (4.6 h) and Poland (4.9 h) report more. So France's fall is not explained by unusually high screen time. - Effort: 6.4/10 vs 7.2 OECD; 7.0 in 2022 and 7.2 in 2018. Effort is "faiblement corrélé" with scores (450 pts for effort 4-6 vs 447 for 9-10). - PISA 2022 Vol. II (VERIFIED, PDF copy of OECD 2023 report): about 30% of OECD students get distracted using devices in most or every maths lesson; 25% by others' devices. Students distracted by peers' devices in at least some lessons score 15 points lower in maths, after socio-economic controls. Students using devices for leisure at school up to 1 h/day did better than heavier users ("Goldilocks"). In schools with a phone ban, 29% still use a smartphone several times a day; bans are associated with less distraction. https://csi.gov.cz/CSICR/media/Prilohy/2024 p%c5%99%c3%adlohy/Dokumenty/PISA 2022 Vol II.pdf - France vs OECD distraction: 58% of French students distracted by own devices in at least some maths lessons vs 65% OECD (SECONDARY, search summary of OECD Students, digital devices and success , 2024; oecd.org blocked). https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/students-digital-devices-and-success 9e4c0624-en.html 3. Reading for pleasure - PIRLS 2021 (CM1): France 514, stable vs 511 in 2016, below the EU average of 527 (SECONDARY, DEPP NI 23.21 via search). https://www.education.gouv.fr/depp/pirls-2021-la-france-stabilise-ses-resultats-contrairement-aux-autres-pays-europeens-majoritairement-452301 - CNL / Ipsos BVA 2026 (7-19 year olds, n = 1,500, April 2026): 18 min/day of leisure reading vs 3 h 01 on screens; 8 min less reading than in 2016. Ages 16-19: over 5 h/day of screens vs 14 min of reading; about one third (mostly boys) do not read for leisure (SECONDARY, AFP via linfodurable.fr, 14 Apr 2026). https://www.linfodurable.fr/les-jeunes-lisent-toujours-moins-surtout-ladolescence-selon-une-etude-55889 - CNL 2024: 19 min/day reading, -4 min vs 2022; 3 h 11 on screens (SECONDARY). https://www.ipsos.com/fr-fr/comprendre-la-lecture-chez-les-jeunes-francais-tendances-et-defis-en-2024 - Read: the reading decline is steepest at 16-19, which matches the steepest test decline (seconde, especially pro) and the boy-girl gap in PISA. This is consistent, not causal. 4. Smartphones, social media and learning - Causal or quasi-causal ban studies: - England, Beland and Murphy (Labour Economics, 2016, vol. 41): scores +6.41% of a standard deviation after bans, larger for low achievers (SECONDARY; working paper figure; published figure not checked). https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:eee:labeco:v:41:y:2016:i:c:p:61-76 - Norway, Abrahamsson (NHH DP 1/2024; reported in JHR online 4 Mar 2026): event study; girls' GPA up, less bullying for both sexes, fewer psychological care visits for girls; larger for low-SES girls (VERIFIED abstract, no numbers; JHR publication SECONDARY). https://econpapers.repec.org/paper/hhsnhheco/2024 5f001.htm - Sweden, Kessel et al. (IFN WP 1288, 2020): no effect on performance (SECONDARY). https://www.ifn.se/media/fcxcel1o/wp1288.pdf - England, Goodyear et al. (Lancet Regional Health Europe, 2025): 30 schools, 1,227 pupils, cross-sectional; restrictive policies not associated with better wellbeing, sleep or attainment; pupils compensated outside school (SECONDARY). https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11850730/ - US, Florida (Figlio et al., 2025): under 1 percentile point gain in year two; US pouch study (Dee et al., NBER, May 2026): close to zero at three years (SECONDARY, Hechinger/FutureEd, 28 May 2026). https://www.future-ed.org/what-the-latest-research-on-school-cellphone-bans-reveals-and-what-it-doesnt/ - Netherlands (ban Jan 2024): about three quarters of 317 secondary schools report better concentration; self-reported survey, not an impact study (SECONDARY). https://www.yahoo.com/news/study-finds-smartphone-bans-dutch-160724853.html - France, « Portable en pause »: trial with over 32,000 pupils in 2024-25; about 80% of participating collèges favourable (ministry answer to the Senate, Jan 2026, SECONDARY); SNPDEN survey (Sept 2025): 9 collèges in 10 not applying it (SECONDARY). No impact evaluation on learning found. https://www.senat.fr/questions/base/2025/qSEQ25120857S.html - Debate. Haidt argues for a causal smartphone effect; Odgers (Nature, 2024 review) and Orben and Meier (Nature Reviews Psychology, 2024) find mixed, mostly small associations (SECONDARY). https://www.nature.com/articles/s44159-024-00307-y - Commission « Enfants et écrans » (April 2024): see our digest, research/09-sante-mentale-inclusion/2026-11-17-digest-rapports-ecrans-ia-elysee.md , section 1 (social media a risk factor "quand il existe une vulnérabilité préexistante"; proposal 17 on phones at collège). 5. Mental health and learning - Link to scores: no study found estimating how much of the French score decline is due to adolescent mental health (UNVERIFIED gap). The Norway ban study is the closest evidence that one lever (phones) moves both grades and mental-health care use for girls. - Covid learning loss (VERIFIED abstract): Betthäuser, Bach-Mortensen and Engzell (Nature Human Behaviour, 2023), 42 studies, 15 countries: deficit d = -0.14 (95% CI -0.17 to -0.10), arose early, persists; larger for low-SES pupils and larger in maths than reading . https://doi.org/10.1038/s41562-022-01506-4 . This pattern does not fit France 2026, where maths rises and French falls. - PISA 2025 family support fell (49% say parents take an interest in what they learn vs 63% in 2022), which the DEPP reads as a return to pre-Covid norms (VERIFIED, NI 26.40). 6. Other explanations Explanation Evidence Verdict --- --- --- Teacher shortages CAPES lettres modernes 87.7% of posts filled in 2025 (88.8% in 2024); about 96% in 2026 (SECONDARY, ministry and press). Contractuels about 8% of teachers in 2024, +2 pts since 2015 (SECONDARY, DEPP NI 26.37); 11.1% in public secondary (Senate, 2024). No study links this to the 2026 fall. https://www.education.gouv.fr/concours-enseignants-de-la-session-2025-463026 Plausible, untested Fewer French hours No source checked today (UNVERIFIED) Not assessable Composition Seconde: 76% GT, 24% pro in 2025 (VERIFIED, NI 26.22). Falls appear in all sectors and both voies; DEPP shows widening social gaps, not a changing intake Weak Test changes 4e test only since 2023, CE2/CM1 recent, so trends are short; DEPP scales are anchored over time (NI 26.21 methodology, not checked) Weak, but limits trend claims Primary maths policy Maths rising in primary, plausibly from the maths plan and new curricula (UNVERIFIED) Not assessed Best supported: an international post-2018 decline, partly Covid, with a French reading-specific layer concentrated in adolescents and boys that matches the fall in leisure reading. Screens and phones are a plausible channel with correlational support; school phone bans have mixed causal effects. Link to our notes (French, ready to paste) (a) Note santé mentale ( notes/sante-mentale/ ) - La baisse touche surtout les adolescents : en seconde générale et technologique, 22,1 % des élèves sont dans les groupes les plus faibles en français en 2026, contre 12,4 % en 2021 et 18,7 % en 2019 (DEPP, test de positionnement de seconde 2026, vérifié). - Elle n'est pas propre à la France : à 15 ans, le score en compréhension de l'écrit a perdu 18 points depuis 2022, contre 14 points en moyenne dans l'OCDE (DEPP, NI 26.40, septembre 2026). - En Norvège, l'interdiction du smartphone au collège a amélioré les notes des filles et réduit leurs consultations pour troubles psychologiques (Abrahamsson, 2024), mais d'autres études ne trouvent aucun effet (Goodyear et al., 2025) : « portable en pause » doit donc être évalué, ce qui n'a pas été fait (à vérifier). (b) Note IA et jeunes, condition « De bonnes bases pour tous » - Les jeunes de 16 à 19 ans passent plus de cinq heures par jour sur les écrans et 14 minutes à lire (CNL, avril 2026) : c'est à cet âge que le français recule le plus. - Un tiers des élèves de 15 ans est désormais en difficulté de lecture, contre 15 % en 2000 (PISA 2025, DEPP NI 26.40) ; ouvrir l'IA en accès libre à des élèves qui ne lisent pas encore couramment risque d'aggraver cet écart. Sources not read / to do - DEPP note of 18 Nov 2026 on September 2026 tests (blocked); OECD Students, digital devices and success (2024) France figures; Beland and Murphy published coefficient; any CSEN statement; French teaching hours over time.

titre: Quand placer la formation continue dans l'année ? Une semaine de vacances ou trois jours par trimestre
texte: Brief de recherche, GT Éducation, 19 novembre 2026. Complète research/10-formation-continue/2026-11-17-brief-formation-continue-enseignants.md (volumes, budget, options chiffrées), qui n'est pas répété ici. Pour la note 1 (service annuel avec temps protégé). Tout ce qui n'a pas pu être lu dans la source est dans la liste « Non vérifié » en fin de fichier. En bref - Presque partout, le temps de formation est écrit dans le calendrier ou le contrat, et payé par le salaire. Angleterre, Écosse, Pays de Galles, Ontario, Nouvelle-Galles du Sud : 5 à 8 journées sans élèves prises sur l'année scolaire. Finlande et Irlande : jours ou heures en plus des jours de classe. Parmi les pays lus, la formation en vacances n'est compensée explicitement qu'en Irlande (primaire), en jours de congé rendus pendant l'année, et en France, en argent (120 € par jour). - La France a basculé la formation hors du temps de cours depuis 2023, sans lui donner de place. Objectif ministériel : 100 % des actions hors face-à-face pédagogique à la rentrée 2024 (guide DGRH-DGESCO, sept. 2024). Les créneaux restants (soir, mercredi après-midi, samedi) ne sont pas indemnisés ; les vacances le sont, mais n'attirent presque personne (0,38 % des journées de formation en 1er degré, 1,39 % en 2nd degré, 2020-2021). - La recherche ne tranche pas entre « massé » et « étalé » ; elle soutient la combinaison. Le nombre d'heures et la durée du programme ne prédisent pas l'effet (Lynch et al., 2019 ; Kraft et al., 2018). Deux traits le prédisent : un atelier d'été intensif (+0,07 écart-type) et des réunions de suivi de la mise en œuvre pendant l'année (+0,10 à +0,12). Un stage d'été seul de 80 heures n'a rien changé pour les élèves (Garet et al., 2016). - Recommandation pour la note : ni une semaine seule, ni neuf jours isolés. Un bloc de deux à trois jours fin août (intégré au service annuel), puis une journée ou deux demi-journées par trimestre et l'heure hebdomadaire d'équipe de la note 1, consacrés au même programme. Environ 35 heures par an, le volume de l'Écosse (35 h) et de l'Irlande (33 h). 1. Où et quand les autres pays placent la formation Pays Jours ou heures statutaires Place dans l'année Paiement Qui décide Source --- --- --- --- --- --- Angleterre 195 jours de travail, dont 190 avec élèves et 5 jours sans élèves (INSET) Dans l'année scolaire ; dans 99 % des écoles, au moins un avant la rentrée d'automne, et 6 écoles sur 10 en placent deux ou plus avant l'arrivée des élèves ; un tiers des enseignants disent qu'au moins deux INSET sont convertis en séances de fin de journée (« twilights ») Inclus dans le salaire Chef d'établissement STPCD ; NASUWT ; Teacher Tapp, The State of CPD , janv. 2024, p. 6-7 Écosse 195 jours, dont 190 avec élèves et 5 « in-service days » ; en plus, 35 h de CPD par an dans la semaine de 35 h In-service days dans l'année, dates fixées par chaque council (souvent en début de trimestre) Inclus dans le salaire Council (dates) ; école (contenu) EIS, guidance ; North Ayrshire 2025-26 ; 35 h : SSTA Pays de Galles 6 jours INSET depuis 2025-2026 (5 du contrat + 1 ajouté en 2019 pour le nouveau curriculum, rendu permanent) La plupart des écoles combinent journées entières et séances de fin de journée ;
